BONG-0001.text: A pizza box needs a corner full of extra toppings. Halfway through, you could change your mind about what pizza you ordered.

BONG-0002.text: A shelf that folds out of the door when you arrive carrying too much. How many shelves are currently on the wrong side of the problem?

BONG-0003.text: A party needs a little departures board so 'leaving in five minutes' can be updated honestly without making another announcement.

BONG-0004.text: What if you could save unused hours from a boring day and spend them on a good one? I'd waste a whole Wednesday for another hour at the beach.

BONG-0005.text: There should be punctuation for 'I know how this sounds, but please let me finish.'

BONG-0006.text: Put a bench in front of a completely ordinary wall and call it a viewpoint. How long before someone sits down to see what they're missing?

BONG-0007.text: My dog watches me put clothes in a suitcase and knows something's wrong. He's worked out packing without ever needing to pack.

BONG-0008.text: A train ticket should suggest one thing to look for out the window. Not a landmark. A tiny side quest for the journey.

BONG-0009.text: A town square with one enormous dining table instead of separate benches. Passing the salt could become a way of meeting someone.

BONG-0010.text: Paint something specifically to be seen through a half-open door from the next room. Would it look wrong if you stood right in front of it?

BONG-0011.text: Chess, but you have to persuade the pieces to move. You can see the winning move. Unfortunately, the horse doesn't like you.

BONG-0012.text: Every meeting should have an empty chair labeled 'the person who has to do the thing we are casually suggesting.'

BONG-0013.text: Browser tabs should get further apart the less they have to do with each other. I want to see the actual distance between my work and the soup recipe.

BONG-0014.text: Make a lampshade from paper windows around a cool LED light. Switch it on and the room looks like a neighborhood after dark.

BONG-0015.text: A shop that sells the one bit that broke. Not the whole replacement thing. Just the lid, the clip, the weird plastic corner.

BONG-0016.text: An alarm that plays your own explanation of why you wanted to get up early. Let's see whether last night's argument holds up.

BONG-0017.text: If aliens judged Earth by what we put in protective cases, would they think phones are the pets and we carry them around?

BONG-0018.text: A doorbell that starts a song when you press it and stops when the door opens. You'd find out who's taking their time by how far you get.

BONG-0019.text: Clothes shops should show photos of people sitting down in the clothes. That's what most of us are buying them to do.

BONG-0020.text: Give someone an unfamiliar kitchen gadget and ask them to demonstrate what they think it does before telling them. Their version might be better.

BONG-0021.text: Soup needs a shoreline. Give me a bowl with a little bread beach so I can decide exactly how wet each bite gets.

BONG-0022.text: A sofa should come with a map of its internal geography. I've lost enough coins in there to justify naming the regions.

BONG-0023.text: Friends should come with instructions. Mine would start with 'not talking doesn't mean I'm upset.'

BONG-0024.text: Write tomorrow's diary entry tonight. Then see which parts of the day you actually managed to predict.

BONG-0025.text: How many words started because someone misheard something and neither person checked?

BONG-0026.text: What if we named clouds collectively while they passed overhead? Two streets over, the same cloud could already have a completely different reputation.

BONG-0027.text: A cat tree built around the one actual tree visible from the window. Would the cat notice its indoor version is missing some branches?

BONG-0028.text: A bus with a 'happy to chat' section. Everyone else gets to stare out the window without wondering if they're being rude.

BONG-0029.text: What if buildings wore temporary name tags for their previous uses? 'Hi, I used to be a cinema' would explain some very dramatic pharmacies.

BONG-0030.text: An exhibition of empty display stands. Could you guess what used to sit on each one just from the shape of the support?

BONG-0031.text: A board game where the winner secretly has to do the dishes. Only one player knows this, and they're losing very convincingly.

BONG-0032.text: A printer with a preview slot that shows one strip of the page before using a whole sheet. Let me stop it when the first letter is already enormous.

BONG-0033.text: When you delete a file, it moves into a village with all your other deleted files. I'd keep checking on the essay I abandoned in 2014.

BONG-0034.text: Make a cardboard version of your room so you can try moving the furniture without moving the furniture.

BONG-0035.text: A bakery that sells dough at every stage. Pick it up before work, after work, or already baked, depending on how ambitious you're still feeling.

BONG-0036.text: What if dreams came with end credits? I'd like to know who cast my old maths teacher as the captain of a supermarket.

BONG-0037.text: Space travel would be less lonely with a screen showing the view from your old kitchen window. I'd cross the galaxy and still check if it's raining at home.

BONG-0038.text: Record the sound of every drawer in your kitchen and make a drum kit. Finally find out whether the cutlery drawer has been carrying the band.

BONG-0039.text: A jacket with a pocket that can only be reached while you're wearing it inside out. Perfect place for something you shouldn't impulse-buy anything with.

BONG-0040.text: Sort your possessions by how far they traveled to get to you. Which thing on your shelf has had the most interesting life?

BONG-0041.text: What if restaurant menus had a page for the meal you imagined on the way there? You describe it badly and the kitchen negotiates.

BONG-0042.text: Put a visit counter on every door in the house. I want to see which room I keep entering for absolutely no reason.

BONG-0043.text: At dinner, everyone tells a true story but stops halfway. The table guesses the ending before hearing what actually happened.

BONG-0044.text: What if photographs captured what you were about to say? Half my family album would be called 'wait, not yet.'

BONG-0045.text: Stare at a word until it stops looking like a word. Then try to invent a better spelling before the original starts making sense again.

BONG-0046.text: Map all the puddles in your neighborhood after it rains. For a few hours, you've got completely different geography.

BONG-0047.text: A guest book for your pet, where visitors write what they think the pet thought of them.

BONG-0048.text: Pack for a trip using a list written after your previous trip, not before it. Let the person who actually went advise the person getting excited.

BONG-0049.text: A fountain with stepping stones that only appear when the water drops. Crossing it would involve waiting for the fountain to let you through.

BONG-0050.text: Write a film where the background extra slowly realizes they're the only person who still has ordinary errands to finish.

BONG-0051.text: Make a treasure hunt where each clue tells you which object to notice rather than where to go. The whole adventure could happen in one room.

BONG-0052.text: Job titles should describe what people actually ask you for. 'Knows Which Cable' sounds more useful than whatever's on the contract.

BONG-0053.text: Loading screens should show what the computer is actually doing. I'd rather watch it find a file than stare at 78%.

BONG-0054.text: Drawer dividers shaped around what you actually own. Stop making the scissors share a rectangle with everything that isn't scissors.

BONG-0055.text: A repair shop window full of before-and-after pictures of the weirdest things they've fixed. I'd stop to look at that.

BONG-0056.text: A notepad built into the pillowcase. Write the thought down without sitting up, then see if you can read any of it in the morning.

BONG-0057.text: What would we actually do if the moon displayed a loading symbol for ten minutes and then went back to normal?

BONG-0058.text: A gig where the band learns the audience's song instead of the other way around. Hundreds of people trying to teach four people a chorus.

BONG-0059.text: If shoes kept travel diaries, your scruffiest pair would probably have the best stories.

BONG-0060.text: Draw your room from memory. Then look around and see which things apparently haven't earned a place in your brain.

BONG-0061.text: Cereal with a separate bag of the good bits, so I can decide which mouthful deserves them.

BONG-0062.text: That chair full of half-worn clothes needs to become actual furniture. A wardrobe for things you aren't ready to make a decision about.

BONG-0063.text: A group chat should occasionally print one message on a physical receipt. Not the best one. The one everyone needs to answer for.

BONG-0064.text: Birthdays should come with update notes. 'Likes olives now. Still gets pasta quantities wrong.'

BONG-0065.text: A guessing game where you only hear objects being put down. A mug is easy. What does a folded jumper sound like?

BONG-0066.text: Someone should scan fallen leaves at full size and tile a floor with them. Autumn, but you can walk barefoot and nothing goes soggy.

BONG-0067.text: Film pigeons like they're in a serious wildlife documentary. An entire camera crew waiting to see if one gets the chip under the bench.

BONG-0068.text: An airport garden you can visit without leaving security. I want to sit under a real tree between flights.

BONG-0069.text: Cities need occasional blank plaques so people can nominate things that happened there but were never going to make official history.

BONG-0070.text: Art galleries should put the first attempt beside the finished piece. I want to know how bad it looked before it got good.

BONG-0071.text: What if the final boss in a game was the tutorial character, disappointed that you still don't understand the controls?

BONG-0072.text: A presentation remote with a 'this slide was a mistake' button. Skip it without everyone having to sit through the apology.

BONG-0073.text: Your phone needs a button that opens the thing you meant to open before you saw the other thing.

BONG-0074.text: Build a tiny podium for dinner-table announcements. Stand a salt shaker behind it when nobody has anything important to say.

BONG-0075.text: Open a shop where every item comes with the story of why the previous owner thought they needed it.

BONG-0076.text: Build a tiny model of a room from a dream and see whether it can actually have the number of doors you remember.

BONG-0077.text: A museum full of unanswered questions, with empty spaces where the answers will eventually go.

BONG-0078.text: An instrument with two handles that only makes a note when both players agree on where to move them. Playing a song would be a conversation.

BONG-0079.text: A scarf with a maze printed on it that only has a solution when you fold it the right way.

BONG-0080.text: Pick the smallest annoying thing in your house and fix it with cardboard. No ordering parts. See whether the ugly version is already enough.

BONG-0081.text: Cookbooks need a second photo showing what the meal looks like when you're tired and missing two ingredients.

BONG-0082.text: A doormat that leaves a temporary arrow in the pile showing whether someone last went in or out. Useful until the dog ruins the evidence.

BONG-0083.text: Party invitations need a 'might come, don't buy food for me' option. I don't want my uncertainty to become six extra burgers.

BONG-0084.text: You should get a trailer for tomorrow, but only the boring bits. A kettle, some stairs, a queue. How much could you work out?

BONG-0085.text: We need a tense for plans everyone is still discussing even though nobody believes they're happening.

BONG-0086.text: What if rain arrived in neatly separated rooms, so you could step sideways out of it and continue the same conversation?

BONG-0087.text: What if dogs name us after the sound of our keys?

BONG-0088.text: A map should have a mode that hides places you've already been, so your own town briefly becomes an unfinished exploration game.

BONG-0089.text: A neighborhood microphone for announcements that don't deserve a whole meeting. 'Found my drill. It was under the other drill.'

BONG-0090.text: Ask five people who know you from different places to describe you to a portrait artist. See if they all draw the same person.

BONG-0091.text: A jigsaw puzzle should come with one entirely unrelated piece. You can finish the picture, but not the investigation.

BONG-0092.text: Meeting-room chairs that rotate toward whoever's speaking. You'd immediately notice when two people are having a separate meeting.

BONG-0093.text: A video-call button that says 'my face is frozen but I can still hear you.' Saves everyone making the same discovery five times.

BONG-0094.text: A pencil holder with a picture behind the pencils that you can only see once you've lent them all out.

BONG-0095.text: Shopping baskets need a divider between 'came for this' and 'saw it on the way.' I want to know where dinner ends and the detour begins.

BONG-0096.text: Imagine getting a bill for all the places you went in a dream. Three taxis, a flight, and apparently you rented a castle.

BONG-0097.text: If teleportation existed, would moving house become easier or would we simply own furniture that was even less reasonable to transport?

BONG-0098.text: An album of background noises from people's favorite ordinary places could be much more personal than another playlist of favorite songs.

BONG-0099.text: Design your outfit around what you need to carry. Start with the pockets and work outward.

BONG-0100.text: Describe an imaginary machine in one sentence and get five people to draw it. Don't explain anything until they're finished.

BONG-0101.text: Decide what you want the last bite to be before making the meal. Then figure out how to eat toward it.

BONG-0102.text: A lamp that moves its light to wherever you last put your book down. The room would keep suggesting you finish the chapter.

BONG-0103.text: What if friends could trade one boring errand each month? Someone else's routine might feel like a short undercover assignment.

BONG-0104.text: Make a time capsule full of things you currently think are too boring to include. That's probably where the actual era is hiding.

BONG-0105.text: What if subtitles included the sentence someone almost said? Every polite conversation would suddenly have a director's cut.

BONG-0106.text: A garden where every plant is something you've accidentally managed to keep alive before. No buying a difficult one because this time feels different.

BONG-0107.text: Paint a pet portrait with the thing it actually cares about. Not a throne. The cardboard box it won't let you throw away.

BONG-0108.text: A suitcase that opens like a book, one layer at a time. You could get to Tuesday without emptying the rest of the week onto the floor.

BONG-0109.text: A public bench with a rotating backrest could let you choose between looking at the view and watching everyone look at the view.

BONG-0110.text: Draw the same mug with your wrong hand every day for a month. At what point does the drawing stop looking like an accident?

BONG-0111.text: Hide an object without telling anyone what it is. They have to figure out both what's missing and where you put it.

BONG-0112.text: Calendars should leave time after meetings for remembering what you were doing before the meeting.

BONG-0113.text: Screenshots need a space for why you took them. I have a picture of a chair that apparently used to mean something.

BONG-0114.text: Turn an old umbrella canopy into a lampshade over a cool LED light. It would look like the room is having indoor weather.

BONG-0115.text: Supermarkets should put everything for one easy dinner beside the checkout. For people who've filled a basket and still somehow have no meal.

BONG-0116.text: A bedroom ceiling could have a map of an imaginary town that you gradually explore while waiting to fall asleep.

BONG-0117.text: Would aliens think we eat plates if the only footage they saw cut off before we started eating?

BONG-0118.text: Make a song using only the sounds of making tea. The kettle can hold a note longer than I can.

BONG-0119.text: A wardrobe section for the person you thought you were going to become. Hiking trousers, club shirt, whatever required a different life.

BONG-0120.text: Photograph the cheapest thing you own like it's about to sell for a million. How much of expensive-looking is just lighting?

BONG-0121.text: A snack with different flavors on either side. Flip it halfway through a bite and see if your mouth believes you're eating two things.

BONG-0122.text: Furniture with replaceable outer corners. Those are the bits I destroy moving it; the entire middle is doing fine.

BONG-0123.text: A conversation needs bookmarks. Sometimes we're four subjects away from something I still had an excellent, increasingly irrelevant response to.

BONG-0124.text: A watch counting down to sunset instead of up from midnight. Would you spend the afternoon differently?

BONG-0125.text: Instructions that change depending on the mistake you're making. 'No, the other end. Still the other end. Put it down for a second.'

BONG-0126.text: Make a velvet case for a rock that fits your hand perfectly. Is it still just a rock once it has its own case?

BONG-0127.text: If fish could see through the back of an aquarium, would they get annoyed that we put the least interesting view against the wall?

BONG-0128.text: A walking route planned entirely around good places to sit down.

BONG-0129.text: Construction fences should have viewing holes at different heights. I was much more interested in diggers when I was too short to see over the fence.

BONG-0130.text: A whole novel told through notes on a shared fridge. You only find out someone moved out because their name disappears from the milk.

BONG-0131.text: A racing game where you design the track while the other person drives it. They're getting closer and you still haven't decided where the next corner goes.

BONG-0132.text: Every project needs a 'we already tried this' folder you have to open before suggesting anything. Include why it failed, not just who suggested it.

BONG-0133.text: A battery indicator should distinguish 'nearly empty' from 'enough for the one specific thing you're panicking about.'

BONG-0134.text: A coaster with a little flag saying 'still drinking this.' Put it up before going to the bathroom so your half-finished pint survives.

BONG-0135.text: A cafe where every table has a different unfinished drawing could let customers contribute one line while waiting for their order.

BONG-0136.text: I miss a house from a dream more than some houses I've actually lived in. How is that allowed?

BONG-0137.text: Would astronauts on another planet keep calling its dirt 'earth,' or would digging a hole suddenly need new words?

BONG-0138.text: Elevator music that finishes exactly when your floor arrives. What happens to the song when someone presses another button?

BONG-0139.text: Socks with different designs on the inside and outside. You'd have to decide which pair to wear after you've already put them on wrong.

BONG-0140.text: Go for a walk and collect questions instead of photos. Try to answer one when you get home.

BONG-0141.text: Could you make a sandwich that's equally good from every direction? Or does a sandwich need a proper entrance?

BONG-0142.text: There's a patch of my house that's colder than the rest. I want a weather forecast just for the gap beside the bed.

BONG-0143.text: Invite friends over to work on completely different things in the same room. Nobody has to entertain anyone. You can still pass the snacks around.

BONG-0144.text: What if you could put an ordinary Tuesday in a jar and open it when you finally realize it was a good period of your life?

BONG-0145.text: Calling a drawer 'miscellaneous' is deciding you'll let future you find out what's in it.

BONG-0146.text: Put a marker where the garden's nicest patch of shade is each hour. A clock that tells you where to sit.

BONG-0147.text: If squirrels could draw maps, would their maps show paths or just things worth digging under?

BONG-0148.text: A road-trip playlist that gets quieter as the road gets confusing. Everyone already turns it down when they miss the exit.

BONG-0149.text: A streetlight with a button that briefly dims the lights in an empty viewing area so you can see the stars. Then it brings them back for the walk home.

BONG-0150.text: Paint the same scene from inside one of the objects in the original painting. What did the fruit bowl see?

BONG-0151.text: Invent a game that uses the length of a hallway but needs no running. Now design a version for the much worse hallway at your friend's house.

BONG-0152.text: An out-of-office message should be allowed to say 'I am technically here but have run out of useful sentences for today.'

BONG-0153.text: A mouse cursor that leaves a trail you can replay. I want to see the exact moment I stopped working and started circling a button.

BONG-0154.text: Build a little room between two books on the shelf. Make the window look out into the wrong book.

BONG-0155.text: Shoe shops need a flight of stairs and a bit of uneven pavement. Every shoe feels good for six steps on carpet.

BONG-0156.text: An alarm with two buttons: 'getting up' and 'I have decided none of yesterday's plans matter.' At least the second one would be honest.

BONG-0157.text: A time machine should have a 'don't let me explain anything' setting. I cannot be trusted to describe a toaster to the past.

BONG-0158.text: A piano where a wrong note stays on until you find another note that makes it sound intentional.

BONG-0159.text: A hat brim that can move all the way around without turning the hat. I want shade where the sun is, not where the logo is.

BONG-0160.text: Write a recipe for a food that doesn't exist. Give it to someone to draw, not cook, and see if you're both imagining the same thing.

BONG-0161.text: What if a tasting menu got less fancy with every course until the final dish was something you eat standing over the sink?

BONG-0162.text: Drawers with a removable back panel for retrieving the thing that's jammed behind them. Why is the only entrance also the bit that gets stuck?

BONG-0163.text: We should have a word for wanting company but not wanting to provide a report on how life is going.

BONG-0164.text: Write yourself a letter you can only open once you've forgotten what it says. How will you know when it's safe to check?

BONG-0165.text: Write a story narrated by a street sign. It can only tell you what passes in front of it.

BONG-0166.text: What if trees could leave reviews of the view? 'Fine for sixty years, then someone put a supermarket directly in the best bit.'

BONG-0167.text: Walking a dog is taking the same route through two completely different places. I'm looking at houses; he's following whatever happened here this morning.

BONG-0168.text: Train windows that show you the name of the village you're passing, not just the station you aren't stopping at.

BONG-0169.text: A room in a shopping center where nothing is for sale. No adverts. No membership. You can just sit there without owing anyone a coffee purchase.

BONG-0170.text: An orchestra scoring someone making lunch live. They need to react fast enough to make dropping the lid sound dramatic.

BONG-0171.text: A card game where the instructions are also the cards would force people to choose between learning the game and winning it.

BONG-0172.text: Spreadsheets should have a 'where did this number come from?' button that follows it all the way back to the person who guessed.

BONG-0173.text: Every website should have one page where there's nothing to do. Just a window you can leave open while it rains somewhere imaginary.

BONG-0174.text: Build a cardboard invention before deciding what it does. Hand it to someone and ask them to show you how to use it.

BONG-0175.text: A service that identifies everything in your cable drawer, then tells you which devices you've been keeping the cables for despite not owning them anymore.

BONG-0176.text: What if dream characters kept living in the dream after you woke up and had to finish the extremely weird conversation without you?

BONG-0177.text: A scale model of space where the walk between planets is accurate. Put the cafe somewhere inconvenient so people really understand the distances.

BONG-0178.text: Record the sound of an old appliance before replacing it. You don't know which household noise you're going to miss until it's gone.

BONG-0179.text: A jacket with a patch for every repair you've learned to do. Eventually you could tell who to ask about a dripping tap by looking at their sleeve.

BONG-0180.text: Frame a dent in the wall and write down how it happened. See whether guests start asking about it instead of trying not to notice.

BONG-0181.text: I want a recipe that branches when you mess up. Burned the onions? Turn to page 46. You're making something else now.

BONG-0182.text: A front door with a little window aimed down at the parcel spot. I don't need to see who's outside. I need to see what they've left.

BONG-0183.text: Get everyone at the same dinner to write what they thought the evening was about. Don't let them compare notes first.

BONG-0184.text: Why do we celebrate starting things but not the day we finally stopped doing something pointless?

BONG-0185.text: A dictionary you can search by what a word feels like to say. I don't know the letters. I know there's a crunchy bit in the middle.

BONG-0186.text: Wind should leave a visible trail for ten seconds. I'd spend the whole afternoon watching it try to get around the shed.

BONG-0187.text: If your dog could choose one smell for the whole house, would you still be able to live in it?

BONG-0188.text: A grocery receipt might be a better souvenir than a souvenir. It shows what it cost to have an ordinary lunch somewhere else.

BONG-0189.text: Put tiny doors around a town, with the owner's permission, and connect them on a map. Let people figure out who could possibly live behind each one.

BONG-0190.text: Take one photo of an empty chair and give it ten different captions. See how many completely different stories the same chair can carry.

BONG-0191.text: Games should save your funniest failure, not just your best score. I want the replay where I missed the entire ramp.

BONG-0192.text: Replace a team-building day with everyone showing one thing about their job nobody else seems to understand.

BONG-0193.text: What if software updates included a little diagram showing where they've moved the button you use every day? That is the change I need explained.

BONG-0194.text: A photo frame with a second photo hidden behind it showing what was happening outside the first shot.

BONG-0195.text: A container shop where you bring the awkward thing you need a container for. Stop asking me to remember how big it is.

BONG-0196.text: A hotel room you can rent for exactly one nap. Check-in shouldn't take longer than the nap.

BONG-0197.text: If your reflection could step out of the mirror for a day, would it finally want to see the back of the room?

BONG-0198.text: Write a theme tune for taking the bins out. Play it every time until the chore feels incomplete without it.

BONG-0199.text: Clothing labels should tell you what happens after an hour of wearing it. 'Sleeves twist.' 'Waistband folds.' 'You'll keep pulling this bit down.'

BONG-0200.text: Ask someone to describe an object while you build it from paper without seeing it. Don't correct the first version. Let them explain why it went wrong.

BONG-0201.text: Ice cream shops should let you taste two flavors together. I know I like each one. I need to know whether they get along.

BONG-0202.text: A mirror that shows the outfit from ten minutes ago would finally let you settle whether changing was worth it.

BONG-0203.text: A birthday card should include one completely ordinary memory of the person. Not a tribute. 'Remember when we stood in the wrong queue for ages?'

BONG-0204.text: A diary written entirely as questions would be fascinating to find later. You'd remember the period through the things you couldn't understand.

BONG-0205.text: Recognizing someone by a cough from another room is a weirdly specific amount of knowing a person.

BONG-0206.text: Hiking signs should say how much of the climb you can actually see from here. I don't trust another hill hiding behind this one.

BONG-0207.text: If a cat could pause us like a video, I think it would mostly use it just before we stood up.

BONG-0208.text: Write a travel guide to your own street for someone who has never been there. Find one thing worth mentioning that you normally walk straight past.

BONG-0209.text: An empty shop window with a picture that gains one new detail every night. People who pass it daily would be following a very slow story.

BONG-0210.text: Make a convincing poster for an impossible event. A cloud-folding class with dates, prices, and an extremely sensible cancellation policy.

BONG-0211.text: A miniature golf course based on ordinary household annoyances: the cable tangle, the slightly open drawer, the sock that won't clear the chair.

BONG-0212.text: Every 'quick question' should come with a timer showing how long the background explanation has already taken.

BONG-0213.text: A keyboard should have a key for the word you can describe perfectly but cannot currently remember.

BONG-0214.text: A coat rack with a tray beneath each hook for whatever falls out of the pockets. Find your change under the correct jacket for once.

BONG-0215.text: What if every secondhand object got a short handover note? 'Excellent chair. Makes one sound at 3 a.m. Still investigating.'

BONG-0216.text: Write down the boring parts of a dream. Never mind the flying elephant. Why did I know which drawer the spoons were in?

BONG-0217.text: What if your shadow was half a second ahead of you? Could you refuse to do what it just did?

BONG-0218.text: Headphones that replay the last ten seconds of the room when you take them off. For the question someone started before checking if you could hear.

BONG-0219.text: A suit you can change into shorts without removing the jacket or standing up. I want to leave the wedding photos without looking like I'm escaping them.

BONG-0220.text: Write instructions for something you do without thinking, then follow them literally. See how much you left out of 'just open it.'

BONG-0221.text: A meal where each bite shares one ingredient with the last. How many bites would it take to get from breakfast to dessert?

BONG-0222.text: A dustpan with a lip you can press completely flat against the floor. I refuse to accept that last line of dust as a permanent feature.

BONG-0223.text: Give your friends awards for ridiculously specific skills. 'Can carry three drinks and still unlock a door.'

BONG-0224.text: What if a receipt told you the last day you'd ever use the thing you just bought?

BONG-0225.text: An apology that includes a drawing of what you should have done instead. Some people would have to get very good at drawing themselves shutting up.

BONG-0226.text: Photograph the same patch of grass once a week for a year. Put the pictures together and see what happened while you weren't looking.

BONG-0227.text: If a goldfish could choose one room to move its tank into, what would count as a good view?

BONG-0228.text: Luggage with a separate pull-out drawer for the shoes. Why does getting to the dirtiest thing require opening everything else?

BONG-0229.text: A public clock that also tells you how long it's been standing there. Your train is late; the clock has been waiting eighty years.

BONG-0230.text: A museum of inventions that nearly existed. Show the plans, then the one problem nobody managed to solve.

BONG-0231.text: Build a board game where the board is an apartment floor plan and all the players are trying to find somewhere quiet for a phone call.

BONG-0232.text: A conference should have a session devoted to things that almost worked, with no requirement to turn the failure into an inspirational ending.

BONG-0233.text: Notifications should eventually expire with 'this probably doesn't matter anymore.' Not everything needs to stay a little red problem forever.

BONG-0234.text: A pegboard where you can stretch out tangled necklaces and move the knots around without holding everything at once.

BONG-0235.text: A receipt that guesses what meal you're planning from what you bought. I'd like to know whether the supermarket has a better idea than I do.

BONG-0236.text: A duvet with a line down the middle that glows when someone pulls too much over. I'd like evidence in the morning.

BONG-0237.text: An alien's dream holiday might be our least interesting quarry. We don't even know which parts of Earth are worth showing off.

BONG-0238.text: A band where each person only knows one note. How many people before you can play a decent song?

BONG-0239.text: A reversible jacket with a boring side and a ridiculous side. Decide which party it is after you get there.

BONG-0240.text: Give tomorrow a chapter title tonight. See whether you start noticing things that fit it.

BONG-0241.text: Someone put an umbrella in a drink and everyone accepted it. Why did we stop there? Where's the cocktail with a little bus shelter?

BONG-0242.text: A chair that looks comfortable from the front but has a shelf on the back for the stuff you clear off it when someone visits.

BONG-0243.text: A party where everyone explains their least impressive skill would be much easier to prepare for than a talent show.

BONG-0244.text: A day you can repeat, but only until you finally do the thing you've been avoiding. How long before you admit it's easier to make the phone call?

BONG-0245.text: The word 'fine' needs different spellings for the different ways people say it.

BONG-0246.text: What if flowers bloomed according to nearby conversation instead of season? Some gardens would thrive exclusively on gossip over the fence.

BONG-0247.text: Draw a family tree of your pet's nicknames. See how far you have to go back to find its actual name.

BONG-0248.text: A map of places locals like for reasons a tourist wouldn't understand. The good wall. The corner that used to smell like bread.

BONG-0249.text: A comic painted one panel per paving slab. You'd have to walk down the street to find out what happens.

BONG-0250.text: Write a short story using only descriptions of what was left on a table. Let the reader assemble the guests.

BONG-0251.text: A trivia round about the people playing. Everyone submits a fact about themselves; the room has to guess who it belongs to.

BONG-0252.text: An office desk that folds shut at the end of the day with everything still on it. Open it tomorrow exactly where you gave up.

BONG-0253.text: A computer desktop with an actual drawer you can sweep everything into. The files stay where they are; I just don't want to look at them.

BONG-0254.text: Make a little flap for the gap under the washing machine. If a sock gets through, at least it'll have to open a door.

BONG-0255.text: Hire three people to admire the shelf you finally put up. They don't need to be experts. I just want someone to notice it's level.

BONG-0256.text: A mattress you could rewind to how comfortable it felt five minutes before the alarm.

BONG-0257.text: The first space station with a cafe would need someone to invent sitting by the window when there isn't really a 'by' or a 'down.'

BONG-0258.text: Put a notebook beside a public piano where people can name the song they were trying to play. I like the idea of checking whether I guessed right.

BONG-0259.text: A belt buckle with a little stand that holds your phone at table height while you sit. Extremely useful right up until you stand up too fast.

BONG-0260.text: Take the brand names off five things you own and ask someone to guess which cost the most. See how much the logo was helping.

BONG-0261.text: A plate with a ramp for getting the last pea onto your fork. It doesn't need to get away every single time.

BONG-0262.text: Make a rug that looks like a floor plan of the house. Then put a smaller rug on the rug where the rug actually goes.

BONG-0263.text: What if awkward silences came with elevator music only the two people could hear? Would that solve the problem or create a new shared one?

BONG-0264.text: Walk the same route once a year and record only what's changed. Eventually you'll have a history of a street that nobody thought to write down.

BONG-0265.text: Describe a meal using only sounds, then ask someone to draw it. I want to know how recognizable toast is without saying 'toast.'

BONG-0266.text: A picnic blanket printed with the night sky, so you can point at the star you're trying to find without waving vaguely upward.

BONG-0267.text: If birds had departure boards, would 'delayed' usually mean the bird got distracted by something edible?

BONG-0268.text: A bus stop should have a small shelf of books so short you can finish one before deciding the bus isn't coming.

BONG-0269.text: A city map showing which buildings share a wall. You could find out how far across town you could knock on doors without actually going outside.

BONG-0270.text: Paint a mural that forms a picture when viewed from a nearby footbridge, but looks like unrelated marks from the street.

BONG-0271.text: What if every game had a 'confused but committed' achievement awarded for spending twenty minutes on something that wasn't an objective?

BONG-0272.text: Important files should show how many times they've been renamed 'final.' I want to know how many previous endings this document survived.

BONG-0273.text: Texts need a turn-taking mode. Let me finish answering the first question before three more arrive underneath it.

BONG-0274.text: Use a ruined book's cover as the cover of a notebook about that book. You could end up writing something longer than what you were reviewing.

BONG-0275.text: A florist with bouquets for very specific apologies. 'Gave you the wrong directions' should be cheaper than 'still haven't returned your car.'

BONG-0276.text: I'd like to hear the soundtrack from a dream without seeing any of it. Would it explain why I thought the staircase was dangerous?

BONG-0277.text: If aliens had no knees, how long would it take them to work out what a chair is for?

BONG-0278.text: A song with a few silent gaps for the room you're in to fill. The same track would come out differently on the bus and in the kitchen.

BONG-0279.text: Work gloves with a ruler down one finger. Finally, 'about this big' could mean the same thing twice.

BONG-0280.text: Draw a tool for a problem nobody has. Then invent the situation where someone would be genuinely relieved to find it.

BONG-0281.text: A restaurant that offers your usual order with one agreed change each visit. How many visits before your 'usual' is something you used to hate?

BONG-0282.text: An umbrella stand should contain a picture of you getting soaked the last time you decided the sky looked fine.

BONG-0283.text: Some friendships are mostly sending each other things neither person has any intention of doing. We are maintaining a shared imaginary lifestyle.

BONG-0284.text: A photo album that records the bad takes too. I want to remember why it took twelve attempts to get four people looking in roughly the same direction.

BONG-0285.text: The phrase 'put it somewhere safe' should automatically generate a map. Otherwise it's just a ceremonial goodbye to a small object.

BONG-0286.text: Could a garden be designed entirely around how its shadows overlap? The actual plants would be the equipment, not the finished arrangement.

BONG-0287.text: A dog collar that keeps a list of all the other dogs it met on a walk. The dog's social life is getting harder to keep track of than mine.

BONG-0288.text: Take a holiday photo facing away from every famous view. Build an album of what the landmarks have been looking at.

BONG-0289.text: A park table marked 'bad ideas welcome.' Somewhere to say the whole thing out loud before spending money on it.

BONG-0290.text: Pottery class, but you make the shape first and decide what it's for afterward. The wonky bowl might be a very good something else.

BONG-0291.text: Play a game of telephone using drawings instead of whispers, but everyone has to draw the imagined use of the previous person's object.

BONG-0292.text: Documents should remember the last thing you were doing when you closed them. 'You were trying to explain this number. You gave up.'

BONG-0293.text: A password manager that keeps a note explaining why past you created the account. I've got a secure login for somewhere I've apparently never heard of.

BONG-0294.text: A box labeled 'might belong to something.' Once a year, put the contents beside everything in the house and see if anyone finds their missing bit.

BONG-0295.text: A shop where you describe a thing you vaguely remember owning and the staff try to find it. Half the job would be proving you didn't imagine it.

BONG-0296.text: The first ten minutes after waking up shouldn't count. I'm still checking which parts of the dream are actual obligations.

BONG-0297.text: What if you could ask one object a single question about everything it had witnessed? Choosing the object would take longer than choosing the question.

BONG-0298.text: A wind chime with a quiet recording button, so you could keep the particular tune the wind accidentally played that afternoon.

BONG-0299.text: Shoelaces that lie flat only when they're properly tied. I'd trust the laces more than my memory of doing the knot.

BONG-0300.text: Photograph your home from knee height. See how different the room looks to someone who can't see over the table.

BONG-0301.text: We decided some food belongs to specific hours. An egg hasn't changed at 8 p.m. We're the ones making it weird.

BONG-0302.text: Storage boxes should have a window so you can stop writing 'miscellaneous' like that answers the question.

BONG-0303.text: A picnic blanket with handles so everyone can move it into the shade without unpacking lunch for a second time.

BONG-0304.text: Would a day feel longer if every clock showed a different time, or would you just spend all day checking your phone?

BONG-0305.text: If you could borrow someone's accent for one sentence, would they recognize themselves when you spoke?

BONG-0306.text: Make a display of things people mistook for shells at the beach. Every object was briefly much more exciting than it turned out to be.

BONG-0307.text: To the spider in my bathroom, cleaning day must look like a natural disaster with a schedule.

BONG-0308.text: A walking tour that starts with an object and follows its story back to where it was made.

BONG-0309.text: A city tour where you follow the sound of the next stop instead of a map. It gets much harder near roadworks.

BONG-0310.text: A comic laid out like a house. You can follow the story from room to room instead of reading left to right.

BONG-0311.text: A puzzle where each player can see only one part, and nobody can point at anything. Find out how useful 'that bit there' really is.

BONG-0312.text: End a meeting by having everyone write down what happens next. Compare the answers before anyone leaves.

BONG-0313.text: A search engine for your own thoughts would be mostly you typing 'that thing, near the kitchen, not the other thing.'

BONG-0314.text: A hanging paper sculpture that makes a different picture from each side. Start with two shapes that shouldn't belong to the same object.

BONG-0315.text: A shop display showing the five things most often returned together. I'd want to know what kind of weekend people keep reconsidering.

BONG-0316.text: A blanket with a stiff little corner you can use as a bookmark. You could fall asleep reading and the bed would keep your place.

BONG-0317.text: A telescope showing a made-up sky with new things appearing every night. People could argue about discoveries without either person being wrong.

BONG-0318.text: A gig of unfinished songs. Every song stops exactly where the writer got stuck, even if it's halfway through a word.

BONG-0319.text: Laundry labels need space for notes from the person who actually washed it. 'The label lies. This used to fit.'

BONG-0320.text: Show people an unnamed color and ask them to name it. Don't pick a winner. Keep all the names next to the sample.

BONG-0321.text: I want a spice rack arranged by what the meal is missing instead of alphabetical order. Less 'cumin,' more 'something is wrong but I can't explain it.'

BONG-0322.text: A mug with somewhere to put the wet spoon that isn't in the drink or directly on the table.

BONG-0323.text: Give every dinner guest one secret ordinary word to work naturally into conversation. The challenge is finding out whether 'grouting' can sound spontaneous.

BONG-0324.text: Save one boring sentence you say each day. In ten years, what would someone learn about you from all those requests for the charger?

BONG-0325.text: A phrasebook for things you can only explain by making a noise and moving your hands. 'The cupboard does this, then the door goes like that.'

BONG-0326.text: A map showing what the land would look like without any buildings. I'd like to see the hill underneath the high street.

BONG-0327.text: A tortoise delivering only messages you probably shouldn't send immediately.

BONG-0328.text: Maps need a 'fewer decisions' route. I will walk an extra ten minutes to avoid changing platforms three times.

BONG-0329.text: A town map built from residents drawing only their own street. Leave the disagreements in, especially where two people think the same corner is theirs.

BONG-0330.text: An exhibition of shadows where you can't see what's making them. Try to reconstruct the object before looking behind the curtain.

BONG-0331.text: Create a tabletop adventure about returning one borrowed casserole dish. Treat every social complication like a major geographical obstacle.

BONG-0332.text: A jobs website where people show you an average Tuesday instead of telling you their job title.

BONG-0333.text: A screen that gets larger only when you lean in to read small text. I want the computer to meet me halfway.

BONG-0334.text: Build a machine with no electronics. The buttons just flip paper signs behind a window. Start with something a real machine makes unnecessarily complicated.

BONG-0335.text: A stationery shop where you have to write one page before buying the notebook. Make sure you like writing, not just the idea of owning it.

BONG-0336.text: What if recurring dreams had optional side quests? Same impossible exam, but this time I'm finding out who maintains the underwater corridor.

BONG-0337.text: If you could turn gravity down in your own house, what would you break before remembering to put it back?

BONG-0338.text: Record yourself clapping in a room before and after moving the furniture. Can someone hear that the room changed without seeing it?

BONG-0339.text: Make a pendant that fits a missing piece from something else you own. Jewelry you might one day have to use to fix the lamp.

BONG-0340.text: Track every place you put your mug in a day. Then decide where the coasters should actually go.

BONG-0341.text: A buffet rehearsal with little food models, so you can work out the plate before putting gravy somewhere you'll regret.

BONG-0342.text: A light switch that shows what the room will look like before you turn it on. Some rooms look better as a possibility.

BONG-0343.text: What if you could invite the version of a friend you first met to hang out with the version you know now?

BONG-0344.text: What if you could spend ten minutes in your childhood home, but the year was chosen at random?

BONG-0345.text: Quotation marks for 'I forgot the words, but this is roughly what they were getting at.'

BONG-0346.text: A garden where you plant a new section every birthday. By the time you're old, you could walk back through the different versions of your taste.

BONG-0347.text: Before replacing your cat's favorite box, copy its exact dimensions. Maybe you've been buying the wrong size of empty space.

BONG-0348.text: A train carriage furnished like a living room. A delay would feel less annoying if I could put my feet up and finish a chapter.

BONG-0349.text: A waiting-room jigsaw nobody ever sees completed. You add six pieces, get called in, and leave a duck for someone else to discover.

BONG-0350.text: Take a photograph, draw it from memory, then photograph the drawing in the original location. See which parts of reality survive the round trip.

BONG-0351.text: A game where you can pause the monsters to ask what they think the story is about might ruin several heroic assumptions.

BONG-0352.text: Job applications should let you show something you made unnecessarily well. A ridiculously good birdhouse might say more than 'attention to detail.'

BONG-0353.text: A phone case with a paper notebook on the back. The backup doesn't need charging or remembering another password.

BONG-0354.text: A measuring tape marked with things you own. This gap is two mugs wide; now I know what will fit.

BONG-0355.text: A shop selling pairs of objects for weirdly specific situations. You have to guess the situation before turning over the label.

BONG-0356.text: A clock that refuses to tell you the time between bedtime and your alarm. It only says whether you can still go back to sleep.

BONG-0357.text: What if a parallel universe differed from ours only in where everyone agreed to keep the scissors? How long would it take to notice?

BONG-0358.text: A musical about assembling furniture. The instructions are the lyrics, and the missing screw gets an entrance.

BONG-0359.text: A shirt where each repair adds to a pattern. It should look more finished the more times you've had to fix it.

BONG-0360.text: Play someone a familiar sound and ask them to design a different object that could make it.

BONG-0361.text: A birthday cake made in uneven sections so people can actually choose a small piece without someone saying 'oh, go on' and cutting half the cake.

BONG-0362.text: A decorative bowl with 'please don't put keys in me' printed inside. See how long it remains decorative.

BONG-0363.text: There should be a reunion for people who briefly worked the same terrible shift and never learned each other's surnames.

BONG-0364.text: We label old photos with who and where, but 'why were we laughing?' is often the information I actually need.

BONG-0365.text: What if you had to physically demonstrate a metaphor before using it? 'Think outside the box' would require bringing a box.

BONG-0366.text: Ask five people to describe the same weather. See if they could all be standing in the same place based on the answers.

BONG-0367.text: If cats could write notes overnight, how much of the kitchen would be labeled 'mine' by morning?

BONG-0368.text: Every town should adopt one completely ordinary object as a mascot. I'd visit somewhere famous for a particular traffic cone.

BONG-0369.text: Lost-and-found photos taken exactly where each thing was found. 'Black glove' tells me less than 'black glove beside the sandwich I dropped.'

BONG-0370.text: Paintings should come with a recording of what the artist could hear while painting. That peaceful landscape might have involved an hour of leaf blowers.

BONG-0371.text: A treasure map that shows where you are but not where the treasure is. The landscape changes slightly as you get warmer.

BONG-0372.text: Name meeting rooms after how long people actually stay in them. Nobody gets to book 'Five Minutes' until they've earned it.

BONG-0373.text: Error messages should sometimes say 'we thought that would work too.'

BONG-0374.text: Keep the broken part after a repair and mount it beside the replacement. People can see exactly what tiny thing stopped the whole machine.

BONG-0375.text: A cafe where the menu gets shorter every time you say you can't decide.

BONG-0376.text: Map the places you keep visiting in dreams. See whether the impossible supermarket is always near the same beach.

BONG-0377.text: A robot exploring an empty house might mistake the junk drawer for the control room. It's where we keep all the bits we can't explain.

BONG-0378.text: Footstep music that changes depending on what you're carrying. Soup needs a much slower soundtrack than an empty bag.

BONG-0379.text: Shoes should come with a picture of their tread. I want to settle who walked mud through the kitchen without lining everyone up.

BONG-0380.text: Make the smallest model you can of a place you love. What detail do you refuse to leave out?

BONG-0381.text: There should be a restaurant where the menu is just a list of textures. Tonight I want crunchy, soft, and one thing that puts up a fight.

BONG-0382.text: A fitted sheet with corners that attach separately, then zip to the middle. I'd rather do four easy things than wrestle one enormous elastic rectangle.

BONG-0383.text: Guest books should ask what nearly stopped you coming. You'd find out which whole evening almost didn't happen because someone couldn't find a sock.

BONG-0384.text: Write a letter to the version of yourself who has just finished the thing you're avoiding. Ask whether it deserved all this buildup.

BONG-0385.text: If you gave your washing machine a name, would you be more likely to repair it or more annoyed when it broke?

BONG-0386.text: If every tree dropped its leaves at once, what would the first ten seconds of autumn sound like?

BONG-0387.text: If a butterfly had to rate every flower it visited, how often would the review just be 'empty'?

BONG-0388.text: A bicycle bell with a gentle 'I'm behind you' sound and a completely separate 'please move' sound.

BONG-0389.text: A pedestrian bridge with a viewing hole above each lane. You could stand safely over the road and watch one stripe of the city pass underneath.

BONG-0390.text: Design book covers from a friend's bad description of the plot. Then compare them with the actual covers.

BONG-0391.text: A cardboard bridge contest where the load is one single grape and the winner uses the least cardboard. No points for building a motorway.

BONG-0392.text: Every new work process should name the old process it's replacing. Otherwise we've just got one more thing to do.

BONG-0393.text: A folder that shows the combined weight of everything it would contain if you printed it. Maybe I'd tidy it before it reached a small wardrobe.

BONG-0394.text: Sofa cushions with pockets exactly where things usually fall between them. The sofa can keep the coins if it agrees to make them reachable.

BONG-0395.text: A supermarket shelf labeled 'you already have this at home.' Fill it with the things people keep buying because they can't remember checking.

BONG-0396.text: An alarm that sounds like someone making breakfast. Give me a reason to get up instead of just making staying in bed unpleasant.

BONG-0397.text: Send aliens a jigsaw without the picture on the box. First contact could be us trying to explain why the lighthouse isn't an animal.

BONG-0398.text: An instrument that only works while you're breathing out normally. Every song would have to leave room for you to breathe in.

BONG-0399.text: Empty your bag and design a new bag around only those things. Don't add pockets for the imaginary organized person you keep shopping for.

BONG-0400.text: Keep a list of thoughts that start with 'someone should' for a week. At the end, circle one you could test with paper.

BONG-0401.text: A kitchen timer that asks whether you actually put the food in before starting the countdown.

BONG-0402.text: A shelf that slides slowly downward the longer you leave something on it. Eventually the thing you've been meaning to put away reaches eye level.

BONG-0403.text: Have everyone bring a photo of something they couldn't identify. Spend the evening trying to work out what each thing is.

BONG-0404.text: What if you could revisit a memory from the viewpoint of a different object in the room?

BONG-0405.text: A compliments book for things nobody normally compliments. 'You always put the scissors back.' Specific enough that the person knows you actually noticed.

BONG-0406.text: What if every tree had a little viewing window showing the space its roots occupied? Pavements would feel like ceilings.

BONG-0407.text: What would a dog put in a time capsule? Would anyone still understand the contents after the smells faded?

BONG-0408.text: Keep the photos you take while waiting for a late friend. Give them the album when they finally arrive on time.

BONG-0409.text: Put a big ruler beside a community sunflower patch. Let everyone predict which plant will reach the top first.

BONG-0410.text: Build a theater inside an empty matchbox. The viewer looks through one end while you move paper scenery through the other.

BONG-0411.text: A scavenger hunt for things that look like they have a personality. Find a smug building, a tired lamp, and a bin that's had enough.

BONG-0412.text: Explain your job using toy blocks instead of words. Hand the model to a colleague and see whether they can find your bit.

BONG-0413.text: Tutorials need a bookmark for the moment you stopped understanding, not just where you stopped the video.

BONG-0414.text: Make a project checklist from removable tiles. Take one out each time you finish a task, until there's nothing left covering the picture underneath.

BONG-0415.text: Receipts should have a space for what you think of the purchase a month later. Keep that bit beside the price.

BONG-0416.text: Nightmares need a complaints desk. Staff it with the one dream character who seemed to know what was going on.

BONG-0417.text: A door that opens into whichever room you last thought about. You'd have to stop thinking about the bathroom before inviting people in.

BONG-0418.text: The silence after a good song should have its own track number. Sometimes that's still part of what I was listening to.

BONG-0419.text: A raincoat with a patch that changes when it's properly dry. I keep hanging up something that merely feels less wet.

BONG-0420.text: Describe a room without naming any furniture. See if someone who knows it can still work out which room you mean.

BONG-0421.text: A takeaway box that unfolds into a placemat with a spot for each container. Lunch anywhere starts looking a bit less like unpacking.

BONG-0422.text: Print a tablecloth with outlines of where people actually leave things. See whether it helps you tidy up or just makes the mess look intentional.

BONG-0423.text: Lend books with permission to stop after thirty pages. I want you to try my favorite book, not pretend you finished it because we're friends.

BONG-0424.text: Which ordinary day would you choose to remember perfectly? You probably didn't know it was the one while it was happening.

BONG-0425.text: Could a book tell the same story entirely through changes to a shopping list? Somewhere around 'two plates' the relationship becomes official.

BONG-0426.text: A nature walk where the aim is to notice the smallest thing. Everyone comes back with a photo of a different bit of ground.

BONG-0427.text: Would ducks think boats are ducks that forgot how to move their feet?

BONG-0428.text: An airport baggage carousel that brings suitcases past you while you sit at a table, like sushi. Waiting would be much less competitive.

BONG-0429.text: A building with a floor you can only reach when you're lost. Could you ever go back once you knew it was there?

BONG-0430.text: An art show where visitors can turn every canvas around and see all the testing, notes, and old paintings on the back.

BONG-0431.text: Let the last-place player rename the town in a board game. Winning gets harder when you have to announce you're marching toward Big Steve's Hole.

BONG-0432.text: An award for fixing a problem early enough that nobody else ever found out it existed.

BONG-0433.text: A device with a physical flag that sticks up when it's muted. One setting I can check from across the room.

BONG-0434.text: Make a sleeve for a plant pot that looks like a building. The plant becomes a wildly overgrown roof garden.

BONG-0435.text: A parcel service that takes an empty box to your friend so they can finally send back the thing you lent them.

BONG-0436.text: A bedside phone stand with a little drawbridge. Raise it when you're going to sleep. Getting the phone back should feel like breaking your own rule.

BONG-0437.text: A future museum displaying today's stuff with confidently wrong labels. A garlic press becomes something they think we wore for weddings.

BONG-0438.text: Make a sound map of your street using gates, drains, footsteps, and rattling windows. No conversations. See if a neighbor can follow it.

BONG-0439.text: Everyone at a party wears one accessory belonging to someone else there. You have to work out which thing belongs to whom.

BONG-0440.text: Rename one drawer, then fill it to match. 'Stuff I need when something spills' might be more useful than 'third drawer.'

BONG-0441.text: Biscuits with dunking-depth marks. I want to know exactly which line is the point of no return.

BONG-0442.text: I've kept a box for so long because it's a good box that it now needs a place to live. The packaging has become the possession.

BONG-0443.text: Whoever says 'we should do this more often' gets handed the calendar.

BONG-0444.text: A timer that counts only the parts of a film you enjoyed. Would a great ten minutes rescue an otherwise boring two hours?

BONG-0445.text: There should be a farewell specifically for people you'll definitely see again in the same supermarket aisle thirty seconds from now.

BONG-0446.text: A cloud-shaped kite with no obvious string from a distance. One cloud refusing to go with the others.

BONG-0447.text: A pet camera with a button the animal can press to send a photo. I'd like to know what the dog considers worth interrupting my day for.

BONG-0448.text: A moving walkway with a side lane full of things to look at. You choose when to step off and how far you actually want to walk.

BONG-0449.text: A street with one lamp for each phase of the moon, lighting up to show tonight's shape. You could find out even when it's cloudy.

BONG-0450.text: Write a detective story where the mystery is why everyone has politely agreed not to mention a completely harmless object.

BONG-0451.text: A game's difficulty setting changes how rude the enemies are, not how strong. Same fight, much more personal.

BONG-0452.text: An office whiteboard should keep the faint ghost of erased plans under a label called 'previous civilizations.'

BONG-0453.text: A website with no homepage. Every visitor enters through a random page and has to work out what the site is for.

BONG-0454.text: Make a cardboard periscope for seeing the top of your bookshelf. Explore the part of your home reserved for tall people and dust.

BONG-0455.text: Furniture shops need a room the same awkward shape as yours. Show me the sofa blocking a door, not sitting alone in an aircraft hangar.

BONG-0456.text: Dreams should let you save right before waking up. I don't need the whole dream back. I need to know what was in the box.

BONG-0457.text: If you could see the route every object took to reach your room, would there be anywhere on the map where none of the lines crossed?

BONG-0458.text: A bird covers night where they try sounds from nearby houses. I'd like to hear the one attempting the blender.

BONG-0459.text: Clothes with a pocket diagram visible on the hanger. Stop making me inspect a jacket like I'm looking for a secret room.

BONG-0460.text: Pick the oldest thing you still use and work out what a modern replacement would do differently. Is any of it something you actually need?

BONG-0461.text: A meal kit that includes one optional mystery ingredient. Cook half with it and half without, then decide whether the secret was worth keeping.

BONG-0462.text: A waterproof notepad in the shower for the idea that won't survive getting dressed.

BONG-0463.text: A group chat where messages can only be sent while everyone else is offline. Would people think more before replying or just write longer nonsense?

BONG-0464.text: Make a scrapbook of plans that never happened. Tickets not bought, trips reconsidered, names for pets you never got. An album of alternate Tuesdays.

BONG-0465.text: Invent a word with a friend, then spend a week seeing whether reality provides enough opportunities to use it.

BONG-0466.text: Plant a garden to look best from a hammock. Everyone admiring it standing up is using it wrong.

BONG-0467.text: What does a dog make of two mirrors facing each other? An endless corridor full of the same dog.

BONG-0468.text: Suitcase handles that show the bag's weight when you lift them. I'd like to discover the problem before reaching the check-in desk.

BONG-0469.text: City guides need a page for places that are much nicer than you'd expect. The good bit behind the car park counts.

BONG-0470.text: Create a self-portrait using only the contents of your bag. Somewhere between the receipts and spare cable, a person should start appearing.

BONG-0471.text: Play charades with ordinary situations instead of films. Try acting out 'leaving a conversation while holding a hot plate.'

BONG-0472.text: A desk that tells you how many times you moved something without using it. I'd like a number for what happened to that envelope today.

BONG-0473.text: Reminders should ask which version of you to try next. 'After lunch' is not the same person as 'before coffee.'

BONG-0474.text: Make a miniature of something out of the packaging it arrived in. See if the box contains enough shapes to build what it was protecting.

BONG-0475.text: A shop selling the prototypes beside the finished products. I'd pay less for the version with the handle in a weird place.

BONG-0476.text: If you dream about trying to sleep, does the dream version of you also want the real version to stop interrupting?

BONG-0477.text: A genie who won't grant a wish until you've made a cardboard prototype. I'd like to see someone mock up 'more wishes.'

BONG-0478.text: A jukebox where people vote on the next song without seeing the current votes. Find out what the room likes when nobody can follow the first confident person.

BONG-0479.text: Guest slippers with an outline of the foot size on the outside. Nobody has to try three pairs before admitting their feet don't fit.

BONG-0480.text: Explain making tea to someone who understands tools but doesn't understand human habits. See which steps you can't justify.

BONG-0481.text: Take a photo of a plate before and after dinner. Judge the meal using only what people left behind.

BONG-0482.text: A removable section of wall used only for moving furniture in and out. Most of my sofa's problems are actually door problems.

BONG-0483.text: A housewarming should include a tour of everything the hosts haven't figured out yet. 'This switch is either decorative or controls someone else's garage.'

BONG-0484.text: The phrase 'a while ago' is doing an unreasonable amount of work in my personal filing system. It covers lunch and several entire versions of me.

BONG-0485.text: What if nonsense words were words whose objects hadn't been invented yet? Somewhere a perfectly good 'flarn' is waiting for an engineer.

BONG-0486.text: Keep a weather diary that only records what moved. Curtains, branches, washing, your plans. Could someone work out the month from it?

BONG-0487.text: Build a cardboard room with everything at the scale of one toy you own. See which household objects already work as furniture without changing them.

BONG-0488.text: Plan a day out looking for one kind of detail instead of one destination. Weird doorbells, wonky signs, houses with huge numbers.

BONG-0489.text: A public noticeboard for small mysteries. Who keeps leaving a spoon here? Why does that house have two doorbells?

BONG-0490.text: A painting that shows the scene five minutes after a famous painting ends. Someone has to clear the table eventually.

BONG-0491.text: A jigsaw with no edge pieces. Where do you start when the picture won't tell you where it stops?

BONG-0492.text: A productivity tool that closes itself as soon as you start doing the task. Its main job is getting out of the way.

BONG-0493.text: A printer that asked 'do you really need the last almost-empty page?' would save me from repeatedly owning a single printed website footer.

BONG-0494.text: Keep the things you used before buying the right tool. The coin that was a screwdriver deserves to be in the same drawer.

BONG-0495.text: Restaurant bookings should ask what you're there for. A first date and an argument about the extension need different tables.

BONG-0496.text: A dream journal with two columns: what happened, and what seemed completely normal at the time.

BONG-0497.text: A spaceship designed by someone who only knows boats would probably have an anchor. What would they expect it to catch on?

BONG-0498.text: Two songs with identical lyrics that tell opposite stories because of where the singer pauses.

BONG-0499.text: Dress entirely in things you forgot you owned. See if past you had an outfit in mind or just kept buying unrelated trousers.

BONG-0500.text: Draw what you think is inside a broken object before looking up a diagram. Your wrong version might be a different invention.

BONG-0501.text: Dumplings with little handles made of dough. Dunk the whole dumpling without putting your fingers in the sauce, then eat the handle last.

BONG-0502.text: A sink plug attached to the washing-up brush. You'd have to remember where you put one thing instead of two.

BONG-0503.text: Everyone brings an ingredient to dinner, but nobody coordinates. You have to agree on a meal before finding out who brought three onions and nothing else.

BONG-0504.text: What if you could fast-forward through a queue but still had to live the skipped minutes somewhere else that evening?

BONG-0505.text: A conversation where you can only use words the other person has already said. The first person gets to decide how difficult the afternoon becomes.

BONG-0506.text: A garden path that takes you to the same spot by a different smell each season.

BONG-0507.text: Would a dog understand a portrait of itself better if the artist included its smell?

BONG-0508.text: A suitcase with its own flat packing mat that folds out on the bed. You'd know whether everything fits before starting the argument with the zip.

BONG-0509.text: A public noticeboard showing things people can lend within one street. Half the drills in the neighborhood might finally meet the same shelf.

BONG-0510.text: Make a sculpture by building only the spaces between the parts of another sculpture. See if anyone can recognize what's missing.

BONG-0511.text: A board game where you spend your turn designing the obstacle the next player has to get past using whatever is already on the table.

BONG-0512.text: A class where the teacher shows the finished thing first and lets everyone invent a way to make it before explaining the usual method.

BONG-0513.text: A computer undo button that shows a short preview of what it's about to undo. I want to stop gambling with the last ten minutes.

BONG-0514.text: Build paper dominoes that spell a sentence only after they fall over. Let someone knock the thought into place.

BONG-0515.text: A cafe that lets you buy a seat by the hour and bring your own food. I'd like to know exactly what I'm paying to stay for.

BONG-0516.text: What if you could return to a dream only by remembering the route you took to get there?

BONG-0517.text: If teleporters became normal, would we still put doors on the front of houses or just choose a nice corner to appear in?

BONG-0518.text: A song where the chorus changes one word each time until the final chorus means the opposite of the first.

BONG-0519.text: Clothes that become less formal as you undo buttons, without becoming more naked. Business casual could be an actual setting.

BONG-0520.text: If every object doubled in size when you called it by the wrong name, how careful would people get with the word 'thing'?

BONG-0521.text: A restaurant where the main course arrives under a lid and you have to identify it by smell before you look.

BONG-0522.text: A mug that tilts slightly toward you as it empties. The last sip shouldn't require looking straight up at the ceiling.

BONG-0523.text: A party where your name tag is written by the person who knows you least. Interesting way to find out what your first impression actually was.

BONG-0524.text: A watch that tells you the time in the place you most recently miss. Not useful for appointments, but maybe that's not what you checked it for.

BONG-0525.text: Why isn't there a word for understanding an explanation halfway through explaining why you don't understand it?

BONG-0526.text: What if tree rings were visible from the outside? You could watch a tree add another year without having to cut it open.

BONG-0527.text: An aquarium with a tunnel running around the room at shelf height. The fish could come and check what you're doing for once.

BONG-0528.text: A holiday where you revisit a place at the hour all your old photos were taken. Find out how much of the place was actually the light.

BONG-0529.text: A pedestrian crossing that plays the sound of the place you're walking toward. Birds for the park, waves for the beach, nothing dramatic for the dentist.

BONG-0530.text: A film where the camera follows whichever character currently has the house keys, even if they're nowhere near the main plot.

BONG-0531.text: A guessing game where everyone describes the same object except one person, who has to work out what they're all pretending not to name.

BONG-0532.text: A history lesson built around what people thought would happen next, not just what we know happened afterward.

BONG-0533.text: A keyboard that grows a new key for a word every thousand times you use it. Mine would eventually spell 'sorry' without involving any other keys.

BONG-0534.text: Make a shelf with a removable silhouette of each tool behind it. Empty spaces become much harder to pretend you haven't noticed.

BONG-0535.text: A shop where the price drops each time you correctly explain what part of the item does. The discount rewards knowing what you're buying.

BONG-0536.text: A dream where everyone recognizes you, but they're all slightly wrong about who you are. How long before you start going along with it?

BONG-0537.text: An alien visitor who learns everything from instruction manuals might think humans spend most of their lives assembling shelves and occasionally becoming very hot.

BONG-0538.text: A concert where the audience hears the soundcheck as the opening song. The tune grows out of everyone deciding whether the equipment works.

BONG-0539.text: A tie with a design that forms a picture only when the knot is right. Finally a reason to check besides being told it looks wrong.

BONG-0540.text: What if you could hear how certain someone was separately from how confident they sounded? Arguments would get much shorter or much louder.

BONG-0541.text: I'd buy a bag of popcorn that started salty at the top and gradually became sweet. The movie snack could have its own ending.

BONG-0542.text: A cupboard where the shelves come toward you one at a time, like a little stage. I want to stop kneeling to meet the saucepan at the back.

BONG-0543.text: Ask a friend to plan your perfect day, then plan theirs. Trade the plans and see whether either of you should be allowed to make reservations.

BONG-0544.text: If you met yourself from last week, how much would you genuinely have to tell them?

BONG-0545.text: A book where every crossed-out sentence stays readable. You'd get the story and all the ways the writer nearly made it worse.

BONG-0546.text: A rain gauge shaped like the local pond. When it rains, you get a miniature version of what happened down the road.

BONG-0547.text: If a cat could open exactly one human-sized door itself, would it choose the front door or the cupboard where we hide the hoover?

BONG-0548.text: Train tickets with a blank postcard on the back. Write something before arriving so the journey gets to be part of the trip.

BONG-0549.text: A town clock with a second face visible only from one very specific window. Someone gets a private clock without owning it.

BONG-0550.text: Draw a familiar object from touch alone, with your eyes closed. Then put the drawing beside the object like it's an honest portrait.

BONG-0551.text: Mini golf where players can move one obstacle after each shot, including when it helps somebody else more than themselves.

BONG-0552.text: A museum of inventions arranged by the size of the problem, not the machine. Some enormous machines would get an embarrassing label.

BONG-0553.text: A camera that takes one photo before you press the shutter. I'd finally have the expression that made me reach for the camera.

BONG-0554.text: A plant-pot stand on a lazy Susan so the plants can take turns getting the good bit of window.

BONG-0555.text: A service that helps you finish the last ten percent of a project without trying to turn it into a better project.

BONG-0556.text: If two dream characters told you different versions of an event, which one would your brain consider the official memory?

BONG-0557.text: If we get hotels on the moon, will Earth-facing rooms cost more, or will everyone be sick of looking at home?

BONG-0558.text: A radio that plays the same minute from different stations around the world, one after another. One moment, dozens of completely different afternoons.

BONG-0559.text: Shoes with removable insoles that turn into slippers. I'd like the comfortable bit to come inside without bringing the pavement.

BONG-0560.text: If a mirror showed the face you expected rather than the one you had, when would you first realize it was lying?

BONG-0561.text: A grinder for chocolate, kept beside the salt and pepper. Some meals would go very wrong before I accepted it wasn't for everything.

BONG-0562.text: A bath towel with a completely different texture at each end. No more standing there trying to remember which bit did what.

BONG-0563.text: A group photo taken from the spot where each person was standing. The album would have everyone else's view except your own.

BONG-0564.text: A calendar that slowly fills in with what actually happened instead of what you planned. By December, it would belong to a different person.

BONG-0565.text: What if proper names had to describe something the person actually did that week? Meeting introductions would need constant updating.

BONG-0566.text: Put a mirror on the ground under a tree and photograph the canopy. It could look like a hole all the way through the planet.

BONG-0567.text: A pet bed made in the exact shape your dog leaves on the sofa when it stands up.

BONG-0568.text: A hotel where your room number tells you how many steps it is from reception. You'd understand the booking much earlier.

BONG-0569.text: A park designed so the walk home is always slightly different from the walk in, even if you turn around at the same place.
