BONG-0570.text: A comic where every speech bubble is slightly too small, forcing the characters to keep interrupting themselves.

BONG-0571.text: A game of tag where the person who's 'it' doesn't know yet. Everyone else has to act normal until they work it out.

BONG-0572.text: A cooking class where everyone gets the same ingredients but a different amount of equipment. Find out what the fancy pan was actually doing.

BONG-0573.text: A phone charger that shows which end is failing. I don't want to conduct another three-cable investigation beside the bed.

BONG-0574.text: Turn an old picture frame into a weaving loom and make something from strips of worn-out clothes. The frame is already ready to hang the result.

BONG-0575.text: A restaurant that serves the side dish first and lets you choose a main to go with it. The chips finally get to make the decision.

BONG-0576.text: A pillow that plays back only the last ordinary sentence you heard before sleeping. See what your dream decides to do with 'put that in the fridge.'

BONG-0577.text: What if the universe came with a scale bar that changed whenever you zoomed out? At what point would familiar distances stop being useful?

BONG-0578.text: A door knocker with a rhythm you can rearrange using little wooden blocks. Visitors have to learn your house's beat.

BONG-0579.text: A T-shirt whose design continues onto the inside. Turning it inside out shouldn't look like the artist forgot to finish.

BONG-0580.text: Imagine a room where every object is the correct size except one. How small could the mistake be before you stopped noticing it?

BONG-0581.text: What if the inside of a food tasted like the outside looked? A pineapple would be a very different commitment.

BONG-0582.text: A carpet pattern that includes one unfinished line. Leave a matching piece of yarn nearby and see how many guests try to fix it.

BONG-0583.text: Friends should teach each other one thing they're weirdly good at. I'd trade folding fitted sheets for knowing when an avocado is lying.

BONG-0584.text: A calendar where days you remember vividly take up more space. An entire school summer might end up smaller than one awkward lunch.

BONG-0585.text: A translation game where you explain a familiar saying literally and everyone guesses the saying. 'This container of worms should have remained closed.'

BONG-0586.text: I want a map showing where the rain that lands on my roof eventually ends up. At what point does it stop being my weather?

BONG-0587.text: What does a bird think a closed window is? The view is right there, but the air has suddenly become solid.

BONG-0588.text: I'd take a mystery day trip where I knew the weather and walking distance, but not the destination until I got there.

BONG-0589.text: Empty parking spaces could have a different drawing underneath each car. The picture changes every time somebody leaves.

BONG-0590.text: Paint a still life, move one object, and paint it again. Repeat until the last painting has nothing in common with the first except the table.

BONG-0591.text: A card game where you score for predicting who wins the next round rather than winning it yourself. Watch how quickly people become supportive.

BONG-0592.text: A lesson where you can ask only 'why that part?' until the teacher runs out of things they normally take for granted.

BONG-0593.text: A website that can be explored entirely by zooming in. The menu is somewhere inside the picture you're already looking at.

BONG-0594.text: A pencil case that unfolds into a little desk mat with places for every pen. Packing away becomes folding the mess into a smaller mess.

BONG-0595.text: A shop that lends you the ugly version of an expensive thing for a week. Find out whether you want the function or just the nice-looking object.

BONG-0596.text: What if the person chasing you in a dream was just trying to return something you dropped three dreams ago?

BONG-0597.text: A planet with a day shorter than dinner would need different rules about what counts as staying up late.

BONG-0598.text: A playlist of people humming the wrong song very confidently. Play the humming before revealing the title so everybody can make the same mistake.

BONG-0599.text: A backpack that opens flat like a cupboard door, so you can see everything without unloading it onto the floor.

BONG-0600.text: If you could see every place your hand had touched in a day, which part of the map would surprise you most?

BONG-0601.text: A dinner where every dish is a different person's idea of what you eat when nobody's watching.

BONG-0602.text: A shower with a foot-operated pause button. I don't want to rebuild the perfect temperature every time I stop to use the soap.

BONG-0603.text: A dinner where you can only tell stories you haven't told anyone at the table before. Some friendships would have a very quiet first course.

BONG-0604.text: A time machine that can only move things, not people. Your first problem is deciding what to send yourself before the machine existed.

BONG-0605.text: A greeting card with a blank space for the thing you both know but aren't writing down. That bit might mean more than the message.

BONG-0606.text: A garden with no straight edges, including the gate. Make the boundary look like the plants were consulted.

BONG-0607.text: A doorbell at dog height that only rings inside the house. The dog can announce that the garden has become boring.

BONG-0608.text: A bus seat that briefly lights up when its occupant presses the stop button. People standing would know which end to shuffle toward.

BONG-0609.text: An indoor public square for days when outside is technically available but nobody wants it.

BONG-0610.text: A film with all the dramatic music removed from the big scenes and added to the boring ones. The trip to buy milk becomes suspiciously tense.

BONG-0611.text: An escape room where the door is unlocked from the start. The puzzle is deciding what would make you willing to leave.

BONG-0612.text: A lesson where the expert can only tell you which parts don't matter. Find out how much effort you've been spending on the decorative bits.

BONG-0613.text: A screen saver showing the actual room from five minutes ago. You could catch the moment you put down the thing you're now looking for.

BONG-0614.text: Build a cardboard lift for the object you're always carrying between two shelves. It can be entirely unnecessary and still make you happy to use it.

BONG-0615.text: A cafe with a table you can reserve for drawing, where the staff know not to clear the weird arrangement of cups you're sketching.

BONG-0616.text: A hotel for dreams where you choose one detail, not the whole dream. Same room as last time, but please let the door open normally.

BONG-0617.text: If aliens asked us to prove we were intelligent without using anything we'd built, what would we actually do in the room?

BONG-0618.text: If you could hear the tune stuck in everybody's head on a train, would any two people accidentally be in time?

BONG-0619.text: A coat made from patches contributed by the places you've lived. You'd be wearing a map nobody else could read without asking.

BONG-0620.text: What if a door opened only after you explained why you wanted to go through it? Half my trips to the kitchen would end in the hallway.

BONG-0621.text: Pancakes with a spiral groove instead of a flat surface. I want the syrup to reach the middle without needing a flood.

BONG-0622.text: Curtains with pockets for the ties, because the thing that holds them back shouldn't become a separate household mystery.

BONG-0623.text: Let the quietest person choose the next topic without having to lead the conversation about it.

BONG-0624.text: Could you describe the current year without mentioning any technology? Which parts would still give it away?

BONG-0625.text: If thoughts appeared as subtitles above your head, would you learn to think in tiny writing?

BONG-0626.text: If a forest could choose where the footpaths went, would it make the shortest route or send us around the bits it wanted left alone?

BONG-0627.text: If a snail could choose a new shell pattern every day, would it coordinate with where it planned to go?

BONG-0628.text: What if you could visit a city only by following directions written by someone who moved away twenty years ago?

BONG-0629.text: Street corners with a little inset showing what stood there before the current building. Not a whole plaque; just enough to make you look twice.

BONG-0630.text: A sculpture that arrives as packing material for a much smaller object. You have to decide which part of the delivery is the artwork.

BONG-0631.text: A game where the dice determine how many words you can use to explain your next move. Six feels generous until you need to apologize.

BONG-0632.text: An instruction book organized by the mistake you're looking at instead of the step you were supposed to finish.

BONG-0633.text: A computer game that uses the scratches on your screen as part of the map. Your oldest device gets the most interesting terrain.

BONG-0634.text: Make a lamp using a cool LED behind layers of torn paper, so switching it on reveals a landscape you couldn't see while it was off.

BONG-0635.text: A repair counter where you can watch the whole fix on a screen, including the bit where the expert has to look something up.

BONG-0636.text: When you dream up a person, does your brain invent a childhood for them, or just the feeling that they have one?

BONG-0637.text: A spaceship with a garden arranged to look like a whole continent from above. You could water the part of home you're missing.

BONG-0638.text: A musical instrument that looks unfinished until you find the ordinary object it was designed to borrow as its final part.

BONG-0639.text: A scarf with a warm section and a thin section, so you can move the weather protection without changing the whole scarf.

BONG-0640.text: If you could temporarily remove the name from a familiar object, would it still look obvious what it was for?

BONG-0641.text: Could you make one long noodle with a different sauce every ten centimeters? You'd have to eat through dinner to reach the part you like most.

BONG-0642.text: A key shaped like the room it opens. You'd know which door it belongs to by the floor plan in your hand.

BONG-0643.text: A birthday party for the day two friends nearly met but didn't. You might discover your friendship was available years earlier.

BONG-0644.text: A clock with no numbers that just shows a picture of what you said you'd be doing now.

BONG-0645.text: A dictionary of gestures drawn by someone watching through a window. I want to see how many meanings they assign to pointing at a chair.

BONG-0646.text: A trail marked by plants instead of painted arrows. You'd have to learn what one leaf looks like to find your way.

BONG-0647.text: A bird feeder with a background you can change to match a tiny film set. Only the feeder is real; the birds keep improvising the plot.

BONG-0648.text: A train carriage with windows in the roof for the boring stretches between good views.

BONG-0649.text: A library window displaying the last sentence of a book without telling you which book. Change it every day and let people try to find the beginning.

BONG-0650.text: A portrait made from all the places someone's hands have worn smooth: a tool handle, a chair arm, the edge of a favorite book.

BONG-0651.text: A racing game where you win by arriving exactly on time, not first. Going too fast is as bad as getting stuck.

BONG-0652.text: A school project where you improve one thing that annoys the caretaker. At least somebody gets to use the result.

BONG-0653.text: A music player with a physical marble that rolls to the end of the song. Shuffle sends it down a different track.

BONG-0654.text: A shoe rack made of removable trays, one per pair. Move the muddy shoes without moving the mud onto another bit of floor.

BONG-0655.text: A shop selling shelves built around the exact collection you bring in. The odd teapot shouldn't have to ruin the spacing of everything else.

BONG-0656.text: A dream journal that asks who you trusted for absolutely no reason. Apparently my brain thinks a talking cupboard has useful advice.

BONG-0657.text: What if the stars were visible during the day, but only in reflections? Puddles would get much more attention than the sky.

BONG-0658.text: A song composed for a room with a very long echo. The room has to finish each line before the singer can start the next one.

BONG-0659.text: A coat with sleeves that roll inward instead of outward. Shortening them shouldn't leave two thick ropes around your wrists.

BONG-0660.text: If familiar objects cast the wrong shadows, would you trust what you could touch or what the floor was showing you?

BONG-0661.text: A freezer drawer labeled 'next week me.' Everything in it comes with a note from the person who bothered cooking extra.

BONG-0662.text: A bin lid that becomes a temporary shelf when open. Somewhere for the thing I'm holding while trying to peel the packaging off it.

BONG-0663.text: Have everyone bring their leftover container before dinner starts. That's the actual guest list for tomorrow's lunch.

BONG-0664.text: What if every lie you told about being 'five minutes away' added five minutes to your next journey?

BONG-0665.text: What if questions stayed visibly open in the air until someone answered them? Some kitchens would be impossible to walk through.

BONG-0666.text: What if fog kept the shape of everything that walked through it for a minute? Early-morning parks would be full of temporary tunnels.

BONG-0667.text: An ant-sized model town beside a real path, behind clear walls. Watch which parts of our layout make no sense to an ant.

BONG-0668.text: Luggage that separates into smaller bags when you reach your destination. Stop carrying the whole holiday to the beach.

BONG-0669.text: A public table with a hole for every common reusable cup size. Finally somewhere windy where lunch isn't a balancing exercise.

BONG-0670.text: A play where the audience sees the room next door to the one where the actual story happens.

BONG-0671.text: A game where you build a creature from random household objects, then invent a habitat it would survive in.

BONG-0672.text: A class where each person teaches one skill in the worst possible way, then the group writes a better explanation together.

BONG-0673.text: A photo app that shows the gap between two pictures as blank space. You'd notice the months you lived through without remembering to document them.

BONG-0674.text: Build a model of a room from its reflections in old photos. See how much space you can reconstruct from the mirrors people weren't photographing.

BONG-0675.text: A local courier for awkward things that don't need a box. I want to send a lampshade across town without becoming a packaging engineer.

BONG-0676.text: A pillowcase printed with a phone screen. See whether half-asleep you tries checking the fabric before remembering where the real phone is.

BONG-0677.text: If two planets independently invented the same game, would that be more surprising than finding out they invented different versions of the same spoon?

BONG-0678.text: A listening party where everyone brings the first song they learned the wrong words to. Wrong lyrics are compulsory for the first play.

BONG-0679.text: A wedding outfit designed to become an ordinary outfit afterward without needing a completely different body or lifestyle.

BONG-0680.text: What if you could lend someone your sense of direction but had to go without it until they returned?

BONG-0681.text: I'd like to order the food from the next table based only on how happy they look eating it. No pointing at the menu first.

BONG-0682.text: Imagine all your furniture becoming transparent once a year. Would the room feel bigger or just much harder to walk through?

BONG-0683.text: Two people describe the same disagreement without saying which side they were on. Let everyone guess before discussing who was right.

BONG-0684.text: Your future self gets to leave you one note, but it has to fit on the back of a receipt. How much of the space goes on proving it's really you?

BONG-0685.text: A word that means 'I agree with the conclusion but not the strange route you took to get there.' I need that one quite often.

BONG-0686.text: A bench-sized patch of shade you could carry on a folding frame. Sit where you like instead of where the nearest tree allows.

BONG-0687.text: A dog toy with compartments that open in different orders. The toy should get interesting again without needing to become a different toy.

BONG-0688.text: A travel guide to the first hour in a place. Where to get water, sit down, and work out which way the pavement is going.

BONG-0689.text: What if buildings could turn slightly to share the sun? We'd have to invent arguments about where the front door used to be.

BONG-0690.text: Print a photograph on transparent sheets, one layer per distance. Pull the sheets apart and the flat picture becomes a place you can look into.

BONG-0691.text: A quiz where the question is easy but you have to answer as someone who has never seen the object being discussed.

BONG-0692.text: A science display that starts with a convincing wrong guess. You do the experiment to find the exact point where the guess stops working.

BONG-0693.text: A charging cable with a section that stays in the exact shape you bent it. Stop dragging the whole wire off the desk to reach the end.

BONG-0694.text: A drawer full of cardboard shapes that fit together into different desk organizers. Rearrange the compartments when your hobby changes again.

BONG-0695.text: A restaurant that gives you a small taste of the meal before you choose the size. My eyes shouldn't be ordering for my stomach.

BONG-0696.text: What if dream money stayed in your pocket when you woke up, but it was only accepted in other people's dreams?

BONG-0697.text: Would aliens recognize cooking, or think we're taking broken plants apart and trying to assemble a better plant?

BONG-0698.text: A music box with a melody made from the bumps along an ordinary key. Every house would have a slightly different tune.

BONG-0699.text: Trousers with a pattern that appears only when you bend your knees. Sitting down becomes the loud part of the outfit.

BONG-0700.text: If your house became ten percent larger overnight without adding any rooms, which thing would you notice first?

BONG-0701.text: A box of chocolates where you write your own guesses on the lid before checking the answers underneath.

BONG-0702.text: An ice tray that releases one cube without threatening the other eleven.

BONG-0703.text: A guest room with a map drawn by the last guest showing where they found the towels, spare charger, and thing nobody explained.

BONG-0704.text: A film made from one second of every meal you share with the same person. You'd watch the plates change before noticing you both did.

BONG-0705.text: An audiobook where someone else reads the footnotes and keeps interrupting the narrator. Let the footnotes behave the way they look on the page.

BONG-0706.text: A garden where the plants are grouped by who gave them to you. Rearranging it would feel like doing the seating plan for a family meal.

BONG-0707.text: Do pets have a favorite version of us? My dog might be most attached to the person I am while holding a chopping board.

BONG-0708.text: A car parked in a showroom with a fake rainstorm outside the windows. Let me discover the annoying wiper speed before buying it.

BONG-0709.text: A playground with a miniature version beside it so kids can show someone the route they just invented.

BONG-0710.text: A film trailer for something that never gets made. Make the audience argue about what they think the missing story was.

BONG-0711.text: A game where everyone draws a machine part, then the group has to assemble the drawings into something with one believable purpose.

BONG-0712.text: Learn a song starting with the last bar and work backward. Every new bit leads into the part you already know.

BONG-0713.text: A webpage whose links are visible only in its reflection in a virtual mirror. Browsing it would feel like learning to use a different hand.

BONG-0714.text: Make a cardboard tool belt for the remote, snack, and book you keep transporting from chair to chair.

BONG-0715.text: A secondhand shop arranged by the problem the item solves, not by what kind of item it is. Lamps and ladders might become neighbors.

BONG-0716.text: A dream where the emergency is that nobody remembers what a spoon is called. Everything else in the world works perfectly normally.

BONG-0717.text: What if space had a 'you are here' sign, but it was so large we kept mistaking the letters for galaxies?

BONG-0718.text: A film score written before the film, then directors each make a scene that could explain the music.

BONG-0719.text: A bag with a removable bottom you can shake the crumbs out of without emptying every pocket.

BONG-0720.text: A mirror showing you from the height you were at six years old. The same face, viewed from a part of the world you stopped using.

BONG-0721.text: An edible menu where each dish's name tastes faintly of the dish. You could decide what to order without asking for twelve samples.

BONG-0722.text: A staircase drawer that slides out sideways instead of being hidden under the stairs. Each step gets its own storage space.

BONG-0723.text: Group plans should include one person whose job is to say what we are definitely not doing. Sometimes that would settle the whole evening.

BONG-0724.text: If you could replay one conversation perfectly, would you pick an important one or one you never managed to hear properly?

BONG-0725.text: Try explaining a joke without naming the funny part. Find out exactly where the listener stops knowing why you're smiling.

BONG-0726.text: Collect drawings of the same hill from both sides. Does anyone agree on what shape the hill actually is?

BONG-0727.text: If octopuses invented gloves, would they sell them in sets or make one enormous thing you climb into?

BONG-0728.text: A walking holiday where the only rule is that you can't cross your own route. Coming home would become the real puzzle.

BONG-0729.text: Bus shelters with two roofs: one to keep you dry, another shaped to make the rain sound like something worth listening to.

BONG-0730.text: A painting designed to look correct in its reflection but wrong when you look at it directly.

BONG-0731.text: Hide-and-seek with a bright object in plain sight. It has to be visible from the doorway; you're only allowed to make the room more distracting.

BONG-0732.text: A textbook with blank pages for questions the book made you ask but didn't answer.

BONG-0733.text: A notification sound that tells you how far away the sender is, without showing their location. Your kitchen sounds different from another continent.

BONG-0734.text: Make a desk toy that catches pencil shavings in a spiral. The more you work on something else, the more finished the toy becomes.

BONG-0735.text: A tiny cinema showing films shorter than the time you have until your next appointment.

BONG-0736.text: I'd like to meet the person my brain invents to play 'someone I've known forever' in a dream. What exactly do we have in common?

BONG-0737.text: If you could put one window anywhere in the universe and look through it from home, how long would you spend deciding where it goes?

BONG-0738.text: A volume knob with a mark for 'can still hear the kettle.' Not every useful setting needs a number.

BONG-0739.text: A button collection sewn onto one jacket in the order you found them. Eventually the jacket becomes impossible to replace but very easy to repair.

BONG-0740.text: What if you could see the exact moment a stranger stopped being a stranger to you? Would it happen during an introduction or much later?

BONG-0741.text: A burger assembled sideways so every bite gets the same layers without needing your mouth to open like a suitcase.

BONG-0742.text: The spare room should occasionally get to be the main room. Move dinner in there and see if it feels like visiting someone else.

BONG-0743.text: A party where nobody explains how they know the host until the end. Spend the evening trying to connect the people yourself.

BONG-0744.text: A photo frame that hides the picture until the date it was taken comes around each year. Some memories would get their own brief season.

BONG-0745.text: A sentence written in a circle with no marked starting point. How many different things could it mean depending on where you begin?

BONG-0746.text: A map showing where the stone in your town's buildings was dug up. How much of this place is actually pieces of somewhere else?

BONG-0747.text: A window seat shared by you and the cat, with a clearly marked section neither of you is going to respect.

BONG-0748.text: A bus that returns everything left on it to a little display at the stop where the owner probably got off. With photos, not unattended valuables.

BONG-0749.text: A public wall where anyone can measure their height, then come back years later to find the mark. The town would keep part of your childhood.

BONG-0750.text: Make a stop-motion film of your desk getting messier over a week, then play it backward as an extremely convincing cleaning advert.

BONG-0751.text: A board game whose box becomes the final level. You thought you were packing away, but that's where the last puzzle was.

BONG-0752.text: A classroom with big buttons for 'slower,' 'example,' and 'wait, what?' Change the lesson's speed without having to interrupt with a speech.

BONG-0753.text: A computer that gives you one physical token for each open program. By lunchtime, you'd understand why the desk and the machine are both overwhelmed.

BONG-0754.text: A kitchen roll holder that also stores the cardboard tubes. Give them a future job before they become a collection with no reason.

BONG-0755.text: A rental service for the one specialized tool you need for the last screw. The whole project shouldn't cost another toolbox.

BONG-0756.text: An alarm that waits until the dream reaches a doorway. At least let me leave the scene instead of disappearing halfway through a sentence.

BONG-0757.text: If you left a trail of breadcrumbs in space, would following it home still work once everything had moved?

BONG-0758.text: A concert where every instrument gradually moves farther from the audience. The ending would sound like the song leaving without saying goodbye.

BONG-0759.text: An outfit designed by someone who only knows the sounds it makes while you walk.

BONG-0760.text: If objects made the sound their names suggest, which part of your kitchen would become unbearable?

BONG-0761.text: A restaurant with no starters, just one enormous middle. You turn up halfway through a meal that's already happening.

BONG-0762.text: A soap dish with a little ramp for the last sliver. Let it join the next bar instead of living a separate, slippery life.

BONG-0763.text: I'd like a reunion where people bring one thing they've changed their mind about instead of an update on their job.

BONG-0764.text: An address book organized by where you met people. One badly planned evening might turn out to occupy half the book.

BONG-0765.text: If your voice got quieter every time you repeated an argument, would you find a new argument or just move closer?

BONG-0766.text: If every stone remembered its warmest day, how far would you have to walk to find a different summer?

BONG-0767.text: What if you could swap senses with your dog for one minute? I'd spend most of it finding out why that one lamp post matters.

BONG-0768.text: An airline map that tells you which bit of your journey would be underwater if you were walking instead.

BONG-0769.text: A cinema exit with a quiet room for the ten minutes when you're not ready for traffic and fluorescent lights again.

BONG-0770.text: A play where the props have to be passed from one scene into the next. The detective can't start until the breakfast scene gives back his mug.

BONG-0771.text: A game where you can buy extra thinking time by giving your opponent more turns later.

BONG-0772.text: A history timeline measured in ordinary people's lifetimes, so you can see which 'long ago' events could have been discussed at the same dinner.

BONG-0773.text: A digital map you can crease and scribble on like paper, then unfold back to normal without losing the notes.

BONG-0774.text: Build a handheld viewfinder that crops the room into different movie shapes. Find out which corner suddenly looks like a film when you hide the clutter.

BONG-0775.text: A hotel that lets you test the pillow before checking in. I'd rather find out now than at 2 a.m. while folding a towel into a replacement.

BONG-0776.text: Dream replays with two audio tracks: what happened in your room, and what the dream turned it into. I want to identify the car alarm's character.

BONG-0777.text: If gravity stopped working on things nobody was using, every junk drawer would become a much more urgent problem.

BONG-0778.text: A song where the bass line is hidden in a second song, and playing them together is the only way to hear the full version.

BONG-0779.text: A reversible rain hat with a bright inside, so someone looking down from a window can see whether you want to be spotted.

BONG-0780.text: A room where every label describes what the object almost became during manufacturing. A chair could introduce itself as a possible bookshelf.

BONG-0781.text: An ice cream scoop that stamps the flavor name into the scoop. Give vanilla and coconut a way to explain themselves.

BONG-0782.text: A tap that remembers how far you usually turn it. I keep negotiating with the same piece of metal every morning.

BONG-0783.text: A picnic where everyone brings the snack their family thought was completely normal. Half the conversation would be 'you ate what with that?'

BONG-0784.text: A clock that gets a new hand every time someone in the house starts a timer. Dinner would look like a small emergency on the wall.

BONG-0785.text: A map of a conversation, with a dot showing where the original question was. I'd like to know how we got from buying milk to ghosts.

BONG-0786.text: A flowerbed planted to look like a mess from the path and a picture from an upstairs window.

BONG-0787.text: A camera following a feather from the moment it falls out to wherever it finally stops. One bird could leave a very long story behind.

BONG-0788.text: A hostel where guests draw one useful thing they learned about the place on the wall before leaving.

BONG-0789.text: A street made entirely of front doors to rooms people can rent by the hour. One kitchen, one workshop, one room big enough for the thing you can't fit at home.

BONG-0790.text: A mural made from small tiles painted by people who each saw only a close-up of the reference photo.

BONG-0791.text: A cooperative game where the goal is to lose in a very particular way, without making the same mistake twice.

BONG-0792.text: A lesson that gets shorter every time you correctly explain part of it back. No sitting through the bit you already understand.

BONG-0793.text: A camera with a second shutter button for 'this is just to remember where I put it.' Keep those pictures out of the holiday album.

BONG-0794.text: Make a flipbook using holes instead of drawings. Whatever you hold it in front of becomes the moving character.

BONG-0795.text: An auction where sellers must give the least flattering accurate description. I'd trust 'table, wobbles unless near a wall.'

BONG-0796.text: A dream with subtitles that disagree with what the characters say. Which version would you believe when you wrote it down?

BONG-0797.text: What if the first message from aliens was an answer, and we had to figure out which question we'd accidentally asked?

BONG-0798.text: An album where each song gets shorter and its ending becomes the next song's beginning. Eventually it turns into one held note.

BONG-0799.text: A clothing swap where you bring a photo of the outfit you meant to wear the item with. Someone else might own the missing half.

BONG-0800.text: Every 'maybe later' creates an object you have to carry until you decide. How quickly would you become a yes-or-no person?

BONG-0801.text: There should be a 'one spoon of everyone else's dessert' option. I want information, not another whole pudding.

BONG-0802.text: A ceiling fan with a blank blade you can decorate so the pattern only appears while it's moving.

BONG-0803.text: Friends should get one purchase veto each year. If they talk you out of something, they have to hear about it whenever it would have been useful.

BONG-0804.text: What if you could pause a good moment but everything you thought during the pause was spoken out loud afterward?

BONG-0805.text: A book you can read from either end. The two narrators meet in the middle and disagree about what just happened.

BONG-0806.text: A beach map drawn at low tide and a transparent one drawn at high tide. Move them over each other to see which bit of land is on loan.

BONG-0807.text: If spiders could choose their web color, would they make it harder to see or start showing off?

BONG-0808.text: What if every border asked you to explain one thing from home that would look ridiculous to someone outside it?

BONG-0809.text: A library shelf that leaves the gap when a book is borrowed. You could see what the town is thinking about by what's missing.

BONG-0810.text: An exhibition you explore with a flashlight. The visitor decides the order in which the picture exists.

BONG-0811.text: Table tennis with a target you're both trying to keep the ball away from. The rally becomes more important than who hit it last.

BONG-0812.text: What would you try learning if nobody was allowed to see your first twenty attempts?

BONG-0813.text: A game controller that remembers how you held it during your favorite game and lights up the buttons you actually used.

BONG-0814.text: Make a cardboard switchboard for assigning household noises to imaginary causes. The fridge hum can be the engine; the creaky stair gets a warning light.

BONG-0815.text: A tailor who starts by asking which movement your clothes keep stopping you from doing.

BONG-0816.text: If a dream character asked what you did for a living, could you explain it without realizing how strange the real answer sounds?

BONG-0817.text: A planet where the ground is comfortable enough that nobody ever invents mattresses. How strange would a bed shop look to a visitor?

BONG-0818.text: A pair of headphones with a tiny external speaker for sharing just one bar of a song. Enough to say 'this bit' without handing over the whole headset.

BONG-0819.text: A jacket that changes color along its fold lines. Leave it on the same chair enough times and the chair starts designing it.

BONG-0820.text: What if the thing you were looking for glowed, but only while you genuinely weren't looking for it?

BONG-0821.text: A food festival where the dishes are sorted by the sound they make when you bite them.

BONG-0822.text: A remote with a transparent battery compartment. When it stops working, I want to see whether I stole a battery for something else.

BONG-0823.text: What if you could see the chain of introductions connecting you to a stranger? We might spend less time saying we know nobody at parties.

BONG-0824.text: Take a photo of the view from the same rented room every time you move out. The final album is all the things you stopped looking at.

BONG-0825.text: What if you could erase one word from everyone's vocabulary for a day? Would people avoid the idea or get surprisingly good at explaining it?

BONG-0826.text: What if the seasons arrived room by room instead of country by country? I'd move the sofa into whichever room was currently autumn.

BONG-0827.text: A pet adoption profile written around the animal's actual daily routine. Tell me how many times I'm expected to open the same door.

BONG-0828.text: A bike basket that detaches into a proper shopping basket without making you carry the mounting bracket around the shop.

BONG-0829.text: A community shelf for unfinished kits, with a note saying which step made the previous owner stop.

BONG-0830.text: A film where the only cut happens when somebody blinks. The actors would have more control over the editing than usual.

BONG-0831.text: A card game where you can trade hands with somebody, but only before looking at your own.

BONG-0832.text: A book of common measurements illustrated at actual size. Open to the right page and put the thing directly on it.

BONG-0833.text: A camera mode for life-size photos. Photograph a coin, print a coin-sized picture, and stop putting rulers beside everything you're trying to explain.

BONG-0834.text: A folding tray that clips to the side of a laundry basket for the objects found in pockets. Keep the evidence with the load it came from.

BONG-0835.text: A cafe with one table for people who want to work on something together but haven't met the other people yet.

BONG-0836.text: What if you could send a postcard from a dream, but the picture changed every time somebody tried to describe it?

BONG-0837.text: If every mirror showed the same place instead of reflecting the room, somebody would eventually try to find it.

BONG-0838.text: A book of songs described by people who can't sing them. 'It goes up, then gets annoyed, then there's a trumpet maybe.'

BONG-0839.text: A jacket lining printed with the pattern pieces used to make the jacket. The inside explains why the outside has that weird seam.

BONG-0840.text: If you could erase one expectation before trying something familiar, which ordinary thing would feel most different?

BONG-0841.text: What would a chef make if you gave them a shopping list written by someone who only remembered the colors of the ingredients?

BONG-0842.text: Why isn't there a narrow cupboard that opens from both the kitchen and dining room? Dirty plates could take a shorter route than the people carrying them.

BONG-0843.text: A leaving gift made entirely of the phrases the person always says. They could finally see how much of them is still going to be in the room.

BONG-0844.text: Would you rather get a perfect memory of one lost afternoon or find out what you've been remembering wrong about it?

BONG-0845.text: A pencil that writes questions in a different color from answers. My notes would reveal how little of the page is settled.

BONG-0846.text: A walking stick with a little removable seat for your bag, not for you. Somewhere dry to put it while you check what's inside.

BONG-0847.text: I wonder which human invention a crow would choose to explain to another crow. It probably wouldn't be the one we're proudest of.

BONG-0848.text: A road sign that shows the next three places you can safely stop, with pictures of the actual view from each one.

BONG-0849.text: A city map that shows the sounds you lose when you turn each corner. Somewhere nearby, there's probably a street that's much quieter than you expect.

BONG-0850.text: Make a portrait of a place using only the colors you remember. Go back later and see which color your memory invented.

BONG-0851.text: A puzzle hidden in a normal-looking receipt. The items are the clues, and the total is where you begin.

BONG-0852.text: A course taught by someone who learned the skill last month, with an expert nearby. The beginner might still remember which bits needed explaining.

BONG-0853.text: What if your online avatar aged only while you were scrolling? I'd recognize some people's hobbies from across a virtual room.

BONG-0854.text: Make a paper sculpture by cutting along every line in an old doodle. See whether the scribble was secretly holding a shape together.

BONG-0855.text: A delivery box with a return label already inside and enough tape left to close it again. Returning it shouldn't require a craft project.

BONG-0856.text: A duvet with a soft fold-out pocket for your feet that doesn't make the rest of the bed hotter. I have one cold bit, not a whole cold person.

BONG-0857.text: A spaceship that measures distance in meals eaten since departure. It would be less precise but much easier to complain about.

BONG-0858.text: A guitar pick made to wear into a new shape. The longer you play, the more the sound belongs to your particular bad habits.

BONG-0859.text: Socks with the date you first wore them stitched on the sole. I want to know which pair has been quietly doing twelve years of work.

BONG-0860.text: A picture that changes depending on which part you look at first. You'd have to describe it before anyone else entered the room.

BONG-0861.text: A cake with the recipe printed on edible paper between the layers. Every slice tells you a different part of how it happened.

BONG-0862.text: A rug with a removable central strip for the dog to walk over after rain. Wash the muddy bit without dismantling the living room.

BONG-0863.text: A swap night for things you've made but don't need. Bring the good crooked bowl. Someone has a perfect use for the crooked bit.

BONG-0864.text: A day that lasts until you finish telling someone about it. Long stories would start to become a practical problem.

BONG-0865.text: A phrasebook for talking to your past self at different ages. The explanation that works at sixteen would annoy you at thirty.

BONG-0866.text: An outdoor table with a shallow clear top that catches rain. Lunch would happen underneath a tiny pond until you tipped it out.

BONG-0867.text: A cat flap shaped like a little revolving door. The cat could change its mind without having to go anywhere.

BONG-0868.text: A hotel with a drawer of things previous guests meant to bring but forgot, cleaned and donated voluntarily. The best travel checklist would build itself.

BONG-0869.text: A public clock that briefly displays the time in the city's twin town. Two places could be having completely different parts of the same day.

BONG-0870.text: An animated film made entirely from the accidental faces you find in buildings and household objects.

BONG-0871.text: A game where the map is drawn by the player who got lost on it last time.

BONG-0872.text: A museum room showing the tools needed to make the tools in the next room. Keep walking backward until you reach a rock.

BONG-0873.text: A laptop lid with a mechanical sign showing whether it was closed by choice or because the battery died. Future me needs the context.

BONG-0874.text: A reusable gift box that becomes a different object each time it's folded. By the third birthday, the packaging has its own history.

BONG-0875.text: A bookshop shelf called 'you can understand this without reading the five books it keeps referring to.'

BONG-0876.text: A bed that gives you the next dream's title before you lie down. 'The Conference' would send me straight back to the sofa.

BONG-0877.text: What if the edge of the universe turned out to be somewhere extremely ordinary, like the back of a cupboard? Would we still build a visitor center?

BONG-0878.text: What if every object made a different note when it was exactly where you usually keep it? Tidying would eventually produce a chord.

BONG-0879.text: A dress with hems you can move between marked positions. Choose the length according to the chair, not just the mirror.

BONG-0880.text: What if every object had one invisible side, but it was a different side for each person?

BONG-0881.text: An onion-shaped container for storing half an onion. Close it and briefly pretend you haven't started cooking yet.

BONG-0882.text: A doorstop that looks like the missing corner of the door. The room would appear to be slightly unfinished whenever it was open.

BONG-0883.text: Friends should be able to borrow each other's confidence for one awkward phone call, with the actual friend sitting nearby doing the hand gestures.

BONG-0884.text: A diary showing only the people mentioned, with names getting bigger each time. You might see a friendship arriving before you knew it mattered.

BONG-0885.text: A crossword printed over a short story. All the answers are in the story, but filling the grid gradually covers up your evidence.

BONG-0886.text: Could you make a fence cast the shadow of something completely different? A row of boring posts by morning, a forest on the pavement by afternoon.

BONG-0887.text: If a dog saw you in a mascot costume, would it recognize your smell and wonder why you'd bothered changing shape?

BONG-0888.text: An airport seating area organized by how long you have left. The people with eight hours shouldn't be fighting for the same upright chairs as everyone else.

BONG-0889.text: What if every building had to leave one brick from the previous building visible? A street could keep its history without looking like it never changed.

BONG-0890.text: A stage play where the scenery gets more realistic every time a character tells the truth.

BONG-0891.text: A competition to build the tallest thing that still fits back into the bag it came from.

BONG-0892.text: An exam where you write the question as well as the answer. The hard part is making a question worth answering.

BONG-0893.text: A drawing program with one shared line that two people can pull from opposite ends. You'd have to negotiate the shape instead of taking turns.

BONG-0894.text: Build a cardboard machine with one handle and as many pointless moving parts as you can manage. The only useful output is watching the handle work.

BONG-0895.text: A shop where you can bring an object and trade for anything that takes up exactly the same amount of space. At least the clutter stops expanding.

BONG-0896.text: What if waking up in the same room every morning was the recurring dream, and all the other places were where you actually lived?

BONG-0897.text: If you left a message on a planet before anything lived there, how would you make it obvious which way up to read it?

BONG-0898.text: A silent disco where everyone hears a different instrument from the same song. You have to watch the other dancers to guess the missing rhythm.

BONG-0899.text: A jumper you can unravel from the bottom to knit matching gloves. You have to decide which part of you needs the wool most.

BONG-0900.text: What if you could see the last place an object was warm? A mug might carry a picture of the hand that held it.

BONG-0901.text: A lunchbox with a removable wall between two meals. Keep them apart until you're sure they're worth combining.

BONG-0902.text: A clothes airer whose empty bars fold away individually. As things dry, you slowly get your room back.

BONG-0903.text: A dinner where the seating plan is based on what people are curious about, not who already knows whom.

BONG-0904.text: What if your shadow aged at twice your speed? You'd get a strange preview every time you walked past a streetlight.

BONG-0905.text: Every household has a name for the thing nobody knows the proper name of. Someone should collect them before we all find out and ruin it.

BONG-0906.text: A public garden planted with seeds brought back from people's own gardens nearby. You could see which parts of the neighborhood get along.

BONG-0907.text: A map of the places a house cat naps, drawn as if they were separate holiday destinations.

BONG-0908.text: A city break planned by someone who only knows what you dislike. No crowded lifts, no loud dinners, and absolutely no compulsory sunrise.

BONG-0909.text: A park path that widens wherever people naturally stop talking and start standing in the way. Design around the pause, not just the walking.

BONG-0910.text: Paint the frame first, then fit the picture into the space left over. Let the frame be wildly uneven so it actually changes what you paint.

BONG-0911.text: A video game where one person controls the character's legs and another controls where they're looking. Crossing an empty room becomes a relationship test.

BONG-0912.text: A repair lesson where the student breaks a deliberately simple cardboard mechanism, then teaches someone else how they fixed it.

BONG-0913.text: A computer folder that shows the first and last file side by side. Find out how far the project wandered from what you thought it was.

BONG-0914.text: A magnetic bookmark with a little arrow that points at the exact sentence, not just the page where you stopped.

BONG-0915.text: A service that turns a complicated family recipe into instructions someone outside the family can follow. 'The usual pan' has finally met its limit.

BONG-0916.text: A dream where you can fly, but only as fast as you can convincingly explain how flying works.

BONG-0917.text: An alien species with no concept of 'inside' would have a difficult first afternoon with an envelope.

BONG-0918.text: A band that writes a song around the one sound nobody can identify in a recording. Name the song only after somebody finds the source.

BONG-0919.text: Gloves with a towel strip on the backs. Somewhere dry to wipe the rain off your glasses without taking your gloves off.

BONG-0920.text: A pair of glasses that makes every straight line look slightly curved. How long before your own drawing started bending to match?

BONG-0921.text: I'd eat at a place that serves the first and latest versions of the same dish side by side. Let me taste what the chef changed their mind about.

BONG-0922.text: A tissue box with a little slot for the tissues you pulled out by accident. Clean ones need somewhere to go too.

BONG-0923.text: Get everyone to bring a sealed prediction of what the evening's biggest argument will be. Open them after the argument.

BONG-0924.text: A family timeline measured in kitchens, not years. 'That happened in the house with the blue tiles' is already how half the stories work.

BONG-0925.text: Imagine captions that describe only what's happening just outside the photo. You'd have to guess the picture from what it left out.

BONG-0926.text: A campsite where every pitch has a frame aimed at its best piece of sky. You book the view before choosing the ground.

BONG-0927.text: A dog show judged by dogs. I'd like to see which of our standards survive the first round.

BONG-0928.text: What if you could see where everyone on a train had started their day, without knowing which person belonged to which place?

BONG-0929.text: A shopfront that lends its window to someone who has nothing to sell. Just something they want the street to see.

BONG-0930.text: A photo series of the thing everyone puts down just before posing for a photo.

BONG-0931.text: A board game played on top of and underneath the table. Move a piece downstairs and you lose sight of what happens to it next.

BONG-0932.text: A history book with a margin showing what an ordinary breakfast might have looked like at that point in the story.

BONG-0933.text: A digital clock with a knob that lets you browse the alarms you set in previous years. Some past mornings would need an explanation.

BONG-0934.text: Make an adjustable stand for the oddly shaped thing you always have to prop up with another oddly shaped thing.

BONG-0935.text: A barber with a mirror showing your hair from the angle everyone else sees when you're looking at your phone.

BONG-0936.text: A book of dream objects, with the impossible bit circled. Most of them would look normal until someone tried to build the handle.

BONG-0937.text: What if each planet had one sound you could hear from anywhere on it? Choosing Earth's would become an argument nobody could escape.

BONG-0938.text: A playlist for a book that changes when you turn the page. Slow readers get longer solos.

BONG-0939.text: A bag designed to stand upright on a sloped bus floor. I've bought too many containers that immediately want to become a spill.

BONG-0940.text: What if you could put one thought down on a table and walk around it before deciding whether to keep it?

BONG-0941.text: A biscuit that's deliberately thicker where people usually hold it. The handle shouldn't collapse before the part you're actually dunking.

BONG-0942.text: A porch roof that projects the shape of falling rain onto the wall inside. You could watch the weather without getting up.

BONG-0943.text: Give everyone one interruption token at a gathering. You can stop any story once, but now the room gets to judge whether your point was worth it.

BONG-0944.text: The next time you move, record the sound of shutting the old front door. It's probably the last time you'll hear it from that side.

BONG-0945.text: A novel whose narrator can hear through walls but can't see through them. The reader has to work out how many people are actually in the house.

BONG-0946.text: If fallen leaves kept their shape but turned transparent, would autumn look more like winter or like broken windows everywhere?

BONG-0947.text: A bird bath with a shallow beach instead of a sudden edge. Every bird gets to choose how much bath it was planning to have.

BONG-0948.text: A coach journey with an optional stop just because the light looks good. No attraction, no souvenir shop, five minutes to look.

BONG-0949.text: A public drinking fountain with a bottle holder so you can fill the bottle while actually using both hands for something else.

BONG-0950.text: A sculpture balanced on a single removable piece. The artist has to explain why that one piece deserves to stay.

BONG-0951.text: A race between paper boats where the only legal way to move them is by moving the tray of water underneath.

BONG-0952.text: A practical lesson where the instructor is only allowed to point, not speak. Find out which tools explain themselves and which absolutely don't.

BONG-0953.text: A video player that shows the scene you just skipped as one still image. Let me check whether I accidentally jumped over the whole answer.

BONG-0954.text: Make a folding card whose drawing only makes sense when it's half-open. The most important part of the picture lives in the crease.

BONG-0955.text: A hotel chain where you can reserve the same room number in every town. I'd develop unreasonable loyalty to the seventh door on the left.

BONG-0956.text: If you could keep one skill from a dream without choosing which, would you risk getting very good at running without moving?

BONG-0957.text: A universe where wishing someone luck transfers some of your luck to them. 'Good luck' would become something you only said when you meant it.

BONG-0958.text: An album with two endings. The one you hear depends on whether you listened straight through or kept skipping tracks.

BONG-0959.text: A shirt pattern made from enlarged stitching, with the real stitches hidden inside the drawing of stitches.

BONG-0960.text: If a room got quieter the more people misunderstood the conversation, some meetings would become completely silent.

BONG-0961.text: What if birthday candles counted down instead of up? Not your age. Just the seconds until everyone finally lets you eat.

BONG-0962.text: What if each room kept the smell of the best meal ever eaten in it? Kitchens would become extremely competitive with dining rooms.

BONG-0963.text: Find the oldest unread message in a conversation with a close friend and answer it as if no time has passed.

BONG-0964.text: A clock you set by moving the hands to where you wish they were. It doesn't change time, but it tells the rest of the house something.

BONG-0965.text: What if sarcasm required written permission from the person you were talking to? Some conversations would need a lot of paperwork before starting.

BONG-0966.text: A wind vane that draws where the wind has been all day instead of only pointing where it is now.

BONG-0967.text: Would fish consider a waterfall a road, a cliff, or weather?

BONG-0968.text: A travel diary written by the person who stayed home. Compare what they imagined you were doing with what you actually did.

BONG-0969.text: What if roofs were numbered as clearly as doors? Birds would still ignore it, but arriving by balloon would become much less confusing.

BONG-0970.text: A drawing with a different horizon along each edge. Turn the paper and a different part of the scene becomes upright.

BONG-0971.text: A game where you score points for noticing when someone quietly changes one object in the room between rounds.

BONG-0972.text: A learning diary that records what you used to think was difficult. Later, you can see the bit you've started pretending was always obvious.

BONG-0973.text: A website you navigate by opening nested boxes. The smallest box should contain something that makes the whole search feel slightly unreasonable.

BONG-0974.text: Turn an old drawer into a wall-mounted display of its former contents. Keep the dividers so it still looks like a drawer pretending to be art.

BONG-0975.text: A shop that keeps your unwanted stuff for a month before selling it. A trial separation from the waffle maker.

BONG-0976.text: A bedtime story where the sentences get shorter as the listener stops answering questions.

BONG-0977.text: A museum of things we would have invented differently if our hands had one extra finger. Start with gloves and keep going until the rooms get weird.

BONG-0978.text: A sound museum where you can hear an old mechanism before seeing what made the noise. Guess first, then open the little door.

BONG-0979.text: A wardrobe challenge where you wear one item every day for a month without repeating the rest of the outfit. Find out which thing actually connects your clothes.

BONG-0980.text: A museum where exhibits grow when people look at them. The least popular object might be the only one you can still fit past.

BONG-0981.text: A bread roll with a trapdoor underneath for adding more filling halfway through. Some lunches need a second attempt.

BONG-0982.text: A set of nesting storage boxes that gets less important as you open it. Inside the final one is the screw you went to all that trouble to keep.

BONG-0983.text: An introduction where each person says what the other one taught them. Even 'how to open this jar' is more interesting than listing job titles.

BONG-0984.text: If time travel had baggage limits, what ordinary thing from today would be worth using your allowance on?

BONG-0985.text: Write a message using only the words printed on the packaging beside you. See how personal you can get with cereal instructions.

BONG-0986.text: A balcony planter built like a stepped hillside. One end of a tiny mountain range above the bins.

BONG-0987.text: A pet memorial made from a map of its favorite route. Anyone who knew the animal could point to the exact place it always refused to move on.

BONG-0988.text: An overnight train with a floor display showing how far you traveled while asleep. Step out of bed onto a different part of the map.

BONG-0989.text: A square with a giant chalk clock everyone can update. You'd find out whether a whole town can agree on being roughly on time.

BONG-0990.text: A film where the background sound is from the same location one year later. Nothing supernatural happens, but the place doesn't quite sound like itself.

BONG-0991.text: A detective game you win by proving which clues don't matter. The aim is to make the evidence pile smaller, not collect everything in the room.

BONG-0992.text: A science fair for questions too small for anyone to fund. I want properly collected evidence about which mug makes tap water seem fanciest.

BONG-0993.text: An email that shows its journey as an animated envelope. I want to see how much machinery it took to send 'yep.'

BONG-0994.text: Put a removable paper floor in your repair tray. The marks and outlines left after a project could become a picture of how you fixed it.

BONG-0995.text: A cafe with a menu of different lengths of silence. Order the ten-minute version and nobody asks whether everything is all right.

BONG-0996.text: What if you could share a dream with a friend, but each person remembered a completely different genre the next morning?

BONG-0997.text: What if the sky had a maximum number of stars you could notice in one lifetime? Would you look carefully or save some for later?

BONG-0998.text: If silence had a recognizable melody, would we still turn music on while waiting for something?

BONG-0999.text: A shoe shop that lets you take a photo of the pair you're wearing out. Ten years later, you'd have a portrait made entirely of what carried you around.

BONG-1000.text: What if a familiar place looked new every time you entered it, but you still knew exactly where the cups were?
